Recheck levels annually if on chronic supplementation.

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are often continued indefinitely for past reflux, ulcer
prophylaxis, or with NSAID/antiplatelet therapy.
Prolonged use increases risk of B12 and magnesium deficiency, bone loss, and
infection (C. difficile, pneumonia).

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Confirm ongoing indication — continue only if high-risk (e.g. dual antiplatelet,
chronic NSAID, Barrett’s oesophagus).
If used for reflux, trial step-down to lowest effective dose or on-demand therapy
after 8–12 weeks.
Check for rebound symptoms before complete cessation.
Monitor B12 and Mg annually if on long-term therapy.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | eTG Gastroenterology | RACGP Prescribing Wisely

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Risk of severe cutaneous hypersensitivity (HLA-B*58:01) in susceptible patients, and
accumulation in renal impairment.
Often continued in residents without recurrent gout or elevated urate.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication and target serum urate (<0.36 mmol/L).
Re-titrate only after acute flare resolution.
Adjust dose by renal function (e.g. 100 mg daily if eGFR <45 mL/min).
Stop if gout inactive and urate consistently normal.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | eTG Rheumatology | RACGP Gout Management

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Can contribute to dehydration, orthostatic hypotension, and falls — particularly
when used with ACEI/ARB or SGLT2 inhibitors. Also hyperuricaemia.
Risk of hypokalaemia and renal impairment with prolonged use.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication (e.g. fluid overload vs maintenance).
Monitor weight, renal function, and electrolytes at least every 3–6 months.
If stable and euvolaemic, trial dose reduction or alternate-day use.
Re-educate staff on daily weight thresholds for GP review (>2 kg change in 1 week).

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | eTG Cardiovascular | RACGP Heart Failure Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Abrupt switching or inadequate wash-out between antidepressants may trigger
serotonin toxicity or withdrawal.
Different classes require specific changeover periods.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
General Considerations When Changing Antidepressants
• Taper antidepressants slowly to avoid withdrawal symptoms (except fluoxetine,
where taper is usually unnecessary).
• Consider clinical urgency when determining the length of the changeover;
intervals may be shortened with close monitoring (e.g., inpatient care).
• TCAs and SSRIs (except fluoxetine) have elimination half-lives of 20–30 hours,
so most of the drug is cleared within 2–4 days.
• Fluoxetine has a long half-life (including active metabolites); therefore, a
washout of weeks may be required before starting another antidepressant.
• Non-selective, irreversible MAOIs maintain enzyme inhibition for 2–3 weeks
after cessation; dietary and drug restrictions must continue throughout this
period.
Category A – Fluoxetine, Vortioxetine
• Gradual withdrawal usually unnecessary due to long half-life.
• Wait ≥14 days before starting the next antidepressant
(up to 5 weeks for fluoxetine, depending on dose and clinical risk).
Category B – SSRIs except fluoxetine, TCAs, Mirtazapine, Mianserin
• Taper slowly to minimise withdrawal symptoms.
• Start the next antidepressant 2–4 days after stopping.
Category C – SNRIs, Agomelatine, Moclobemide, Reboxetine
• SNRIs require tapering to prevent withdrawal; others have minimal withdrawal
risk.
• Wait 1–2 days before starting the next antidepressant.
• Agomelatine may be started immediately when switching from an SSRI or SNRI.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH Antidepressant Changeover Table | RACGP Depression Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Metformin commonly causes gastrointestinal intolerance, including diarrhoea,
cramping, bloating, and nausea—effects that may worsen with ageing, dehydration,
or polypharmacy. Chronic use may also contribute to vitamin B12 deficiency. Renal
impairment increases the risk of drug accumulation and intolerance.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Dose adjustment based on renal function (Aronoff et al. + manufacturer guidance):
• eGFR 45–59 mL/min
• Use 25–50% of usual dose.
• Maximum 2,000 mg/day in 2–3 divided doses.
• eGFR 30–44 mL/min
• Use ≤25% of usual dose.
• Manufacturer maximum: 1,000 mg/day.
• eGFR 10–45 mL/min (general Aronoff guidance)
• 25% of usual dose (consult specialist if continuing).
• eGFR <10 mL/min
• Avoid metformin.
If diarrhoea persists, consider switching to Metformin XR or dose reduction.
Monitor B12 levels with long-term therapy.
Ensure eGFR ≥30 mL/min before continuing therapy and review dose if renal
function declines.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH, The Renal Drug Database

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Often used off-label for insomnia or BPSD.
Associated with daytime sedation, orthostatic hypotension, confusion, and increased
falls risk, especially in older adults.
If used for BPSD, it is considered a chemical restraint unless clearly documented as
therapeutic use for a diagnosed psychotic disorder.
Regular review is required under quality standards.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
• Confirm and document indication (BPSD vs psychosis vs insomnia).
• Avoid routine use for insomnia—non-pharmacological strategies preferred.
• If used for BPSD, ensure:
– documented clinical rationale
– behavioural assessment
– consent or best-interest decision completed
– regular review dates recorded
• Monitor for sedation, postural drop, falls, and metabolic effects.
• Consider gradual dose reduction if symptoms stable.

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Long-term use requires monitoring due to pulmonary, thyroid, and hepatic toxicity.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Check TSH, LFTs, and chest X-ray every 6–12 months.
Review ongoing need if arrhythmia remains stable.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: Therapeutic Guidelines; AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Allopurinol requires dose reduction in renal impairment to minimise the risk of
allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome (AHS), which is more common in older adults
and with high starting doses.
Over-treatment is common—ongoing therapy may not be needed if there are no
recent gout flares or uric acid levels are controlled.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Adjust dose according to eGFR/CrCl:
• GFR 20–50 mL/min:
100–200 mg daily initially; titrate according to uric acid and response.
• GFR 10–20 mL/min:
100 mg on alternate days – 100 mg daily initially; titrate cautiously.
• GFR <10 mL/min:
100 mg three times per week – or 100 mg on alternate days initially; titrate
according to response and specialist guidance.
Review ongoing need:
• Cease if no recent gout flares and serum uric acid is <0.36 mmol/L without
symptoms.
• Start low and titrate slowly (“start low, go slow”) to reduce hypersensitivity risk.
• Monitor renal function and uric acid regularly.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH, The Renal Drug Database

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
May be continued in older adults without a clear cardiovascular indication,
particularly when used only for primary prevention.
In frail residents or those with limited life expectancy, benefits are minimal while
risks—myalgia, fatigue, falls, cognitive decline concerns, and polypharmacy burden—
may be more significant.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
• Confirm indication (primary vs secondary prevention).
• For primary prevention in frail residents with limited life expectancy, consider dose
reduction or cessation.
• Continue in secondary prevention only if well-tolerated and consistent with goals
of care.
• Monitor for muscle aches, weakness, liver enzyme abnormalities, and potential
drug interactions.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: RACGP; AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Bleeding risk increases in older adults, especially with renal impairment, low body
weight, concurrent NSAIDs/antiplatelets, or frailty. Incorrect dosing is common.
Apixaban exposure (AUC) increases progressively as renal function declines (mild
↑16%, moderate ↑29%, severe ↑44%).
Limited evidence supports its use in CKD4–5, and caution is required for dialysis
patients.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
1. Dose adjustment by GFR
GFR 30–50 mL/min
• Dose as per normal renal function, but use with caution due to increased exposure.
GFR 15–30 mL/min
• Non-AF indications (DVT/PE treatment or prophylaxis):
Dose as per normal renal function; use with caution.
• Atrial Fibrillation:
2.5 mg twice daily.
GFR <15 mL/min
• Non-AF indications:
Dose as per normal renal function; use with extreme caution (limited evidence).
• Atrial Fibrillation:
2.5 mg twice daily; specialist review advised.
Manufacturer does not recommend use due to lack of safety data.
2. When to avoid or seek specialist input
• Severe renal impairment (CrCl <15)
• ESRD on dialysis (highly limited evidence; AHA/ASA do not recommend for AF
stroke prevention)
• Acute kidney injury
• High bleeding risk (frailty, falls, anaemia)
• Conditions such as nephrotic syndrome or antiphospholipid syndrome (optional
note)
3. Gastroprotection
Indicated if: age ≥65, anticoagulant therapy, NSAID/antiplatelet use, previous GI
bleed, frailty.
Pantoprazole for GI protection:
• 20 mg once daily (standard prophylactic dose)
• 40 mg once daily if high risk or symptomatic GORD
4. Monitoring & Safety Notes
• Check eGFR every 3–6 months in older adults or if renal function is borderline.
• Watch for signs of bleeding (bruising, melena, haematuria).
• Avoid NSAIDs where possible.
• Haemodialysis removes only 14% of apixaban and does not reliably clear the drug.
• AUC for 2.5 mg BD in dialysis patients approximates exposure of 5 mg BD in
normal renal function.
References:
AMH, Product Information, AHA/ASA, renal dosing data (Aronoff et al.), PK studies
on apixaban in CKD & dialysis.

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Digoxin has a narrow therapeutic index and is highly prone to accumulation in renal
impairment, older age, dehydration, and electrolyte disturbances.
Often continued long-term without reassessing indication, particularly in AF where
benefit may be limited.
Toxicity risk increases with hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, hypercalcaemia, and
declining renal function.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
1. Confirm Indication
• Atrial Fibrillation (rate control)
• Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
• If no clear benefit → consider dose reduction or cessation.
2. Dose Adjustment by Renal Function
GFR 20–50 mL/min:
• 125–250 micrograms daily
• Titrate to response and heart rate.
GFR 10–20 mL/min:
• 125–250 micrograms daily
• Monitor serum levels closely.
GFR <10 mL/min:
• 62.5 micrograms daily or on alternate days
• Careful monitoring – drug accumulation common.
Digitalisation:
• Total loading 750 micrograms–1 mg; extend intervals between doses in renal
impairment.
Changing routes:
• When switching oral → IV, reduce dose by one-third.
3. Monitoring Requirements
• Serum digoxin levels:
– Target 0.8–2.0 ng/mL (0.8–1.2 preferred in older adults).
– Take sample ≥8 hours after dose (ideally morning pre-dose).
• Check eGFR regularly (declines quickly in older adults).
• Monitor:
– Potassium
– Magnesium
– Calcium
– Thyroid function
• Review for symptoms of toxicity: nausea, anorexia, confusion, visual disturbances
(yellow/green halos), bradycardia.
4. Special Considerations in CKD & Dialysis
• Volume of distribution and clearance are reduced → high risk of accumulation.
• Only ~3% of a dose removed by 5-hour haemodialysis → dialysis does NOT clear
digoxin.
• Concomitant phosphate binders reduce absorption by ~25%.
• Case reports show severe toxicity even at 62.5 micrograms daily in haemodialysis
when residual renal function declines.
5. Deprescribing Considerations
• Cease if AF adequately controlled on beta-blocker alone.
• Cease in frail adults with bradycardia, hypotension, falls, or poor oral intake.
• Tapering usually unnecessary, but monitor pulse and symptoms.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text:
AMH; Aronoff Renal Dosing; BMJ Drug & Therapeutics Bulletin; Heart Failure/Atrial
Fibrillation guidelines; AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
PRN use for sleep may lead to dependence, sedation, and increased fall risk.
Often used in aged care without documented sleep disorder.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review frequency and indication. Cease or trial non-pharmacological sleep strategies
first.
Document consent and assess effectiveness if used.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; TGA

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Antipsychotic often used for BPSD without formal diagnosis.
Increases fall risk, stroke risk, and sedation in elderly.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication and trial reduction if possible.
Document consent and monitor for side effects.
Avoid long-term use unless clearly indicated.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Psychotropic Prescribing Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Long-term regular use may not be necessary in residents with stable pain or reduced
communication.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review ongoing need. Trial PRN use if pain appears controlled.
Switch to liquid or crushed IR formulation if MR is unsuitable for administration.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: May be continued indefinitely without monitoring or clear indication.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review vitamin D levels and ensure indication is still valid (e.g. osteoporosis,
deficiency).
Cease if levels are adequate and no active bone protection needed.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Osmotic laxative. May contribute to hyponatraemia (low sodium) or dehydration in
frail residents, especially with poor oral intake or excessive dosing.
Loose stools may worsen electrolyte losses.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
• Use as first-line regular agent; adjust dose based on stool form.
• Encourage adequate fluid intake.
• Avoid routine combination with lactulose.
Electrolyte Management
If sodium is LOW (hyponatraemia):
• Reduce Movicol dose or switch to PRN only.
• Limit fluid overload if dilutional; monitor oral intake.
• Treat dehydration if present (oral fluids or IV as appropriate).
• Recheck sodium in 1–2 weeks.
If potassium is LOW:
• Assess for diarrhoea; reduce dose if loose stools.
• Review diuretics; consider potassium supplementation.
• Recheck UECs within 1 week.
If sodium is HIGH (rare):
• Ensure resident hydrated; adjust Movicol dose appropriately.

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Stimulant laxative causing hypokalaemia from increased stool losses. May lead to
diarrhoea, cramping, dehydration, and falls if used daily or with diuretics.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
• Use PRN only, avoid daily long-term use.
• Do not combine with other stimulants (senna/bisacodyl).
• Reduce or cease if loose stools develop.
Electrolyte Management
If potassium is LOW (hypokalaemia):
• Reduce or stop sodium picosulfate.
• Increase dietary potassium (bananas, potatoes), or supplement if required.
• Review other meds (frusemide, prednisolone).
• Recheck UECs within 2–7 days depending on severity.
If sodium is LOW:
• Assess for diarrhoea and dehydration; treat accordingly.
• Increase hydration and reduce stimulant laxatives.
If potassium is HIGH (rare):
• Review ACE inhibitors, spironolactone; this is not caused by sodium
picosulfate.

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Main effect is from senna, which can cause hypokalaemia, diarrhoea, and
dependency if used chronically.
Often continued without review.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
• Prefer PRN use only.
• Cease or reduce if stools are already soft.
• Rationalise with other laxatives to avoid duplication.
Electrolyte Management
If potassium is LOW:
• Reduce or cease senna component.
• Increase oral potassium or supplement if indicated.
• Review diuretics or other contributing meds.
• Recheck UECs within 1 week.
If sodium is LOW:
• Assess hydration; increase oral fluids.
• Reduce stimulant laxative use and treat diarrhoea.
If potassium is HIGH (rare):
• Review spironolactone/ACE inhibitors; senna does not cause hyperkalaemia.

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Osmotic laxative that may cause hyponatraemia, bloating, and diarrhoea.
Effectiveness depends on adequate hydration.
Risk of dehydration and electrolyte imbalance if overused.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
• Confirm indication (constipation vs hepatic encephalopathy).
• Adjust dose to achieve soft formed stools.
• Avoid routine daily combination with Movicol.
Electrolyte Management
If sodium is LOW (hyponatraemia):
• Reduce lactulose dose; avoid excessive water consumption with each dose.
• Treat dehydration if present.
• Recheck UECs within 1–2 weeks.
• If used for hepatic encephalopathy, balance dose carefully (aim for 2–3 soft
stools/day).
If potassium is LOW:
• Assess for diarrhoea; reduce dose.
• Supplement potassium if required.
• Recheck UECs within 1 week.
If sodium is HIGH:
• Encourage hydration; recheck if symptomatic.
Electrolyte Management Guidance:
Hypokalaemia is most often caused by stimulant laxatives (senna, sodium picosulfate)
or diarrhoea. Reduce stimulant use, treat diarrhoea, review diuretics, and supplement
potassium if required.
Hyponatraemia can occur with lactulose or high-dose Movicol, especially in frail
residents with poor fluid intake. Reduce osmotic laxatives, manage hydration, and
recheck UECs.
Reassess renal function and electrolytes every 3–6 months, or sooner if symptomatic,
frail, dehydrated, or when laxative doses change.

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Used for insomnia in dementia patients with mixed evidence and off-label use.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure indication is documented.
Trial non-pharmacological sleep strategies.
If continued, assess benefit over time.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; TGA

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Risk of bruising, bleeding, and falls in older adults. Often continued longer than
required post-op.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication, dose, and duration. Cease if prophylaxis period has passed.
Check renal function for dose adjustment if used long-term.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: Therapeutic Guidelines; AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Used long-term for seizure or mood disorders; risks include sedation, liver toxicity,
and drug interactions.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication and monitoring (LFTs, sodium).
Ensure ongoing need is confirmed, especially in residents with no recent episodes.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; TGA

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
High bleeding risk, interactions with food and other drugs. Requires frequent INR
monitoring.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication and INR control history.
Consider switching to DOAC if monitoring is problematic and no contraindications.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: Therapeutic Guidelines; AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Used as a sedative but can impair cognition and mobility; risk of falls.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review frequency and benefit.
Trial cessation or reduce dose. Use only short-term with review.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Often prescribed long-term without confirmed deficiency or clear benefit.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review dietary intake and relevant pathology.
Cease if resident has stable nutrition and no diagnosed deficiency.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Limited benefit in older adults without cardiovascular disease. May increase bleeding
risk.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Cease if used for primary prevention or non-specific reasons.
Ensure GP is aware if concurrently used with anticoagulants or antiplatelets.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; RACGP Choosing Wisely

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Used off-label in aged care for pain or BPSD. Limited evidence, sedation risk.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication and response.
Ensure specialist involvement and documented consent.
Monitor for adverse effects (falls, confusion, appetite changes).

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: TGA; AMH; Australian Prescriber

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Often used adjunctively for statin-related muscle pain, though evidence is variable.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review ongoing need, especially if statin ceased or well tolerated.
Cease if no clear benefit.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; NPS MedicineWise

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Marketed for neuropathy or metabolic health, but limited clinical backing in elderly.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review with GP if used long-term.
Cease if no clinical response or used for general wellness.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: Complementary Medicine Summary; AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Can cause systemic beta-blocker effects (bradycardia, hypotension). Often continued
without IOP review.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure ophthalmology follow-up is current.
Check for bradycardia or fatigue. Consider GP review if no recent IOP readings or
concerns noted.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Therapeutic Guidelines – Eye

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Frequently used for osteoarthritis despite limited evidence in advanced age.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication and benefit. Cease if no measurable improvement or if used
alongside other OA agents without additive effect.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: RACGP OA Guidelines; AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Can cause orthostatic hypotension and urinary retention. May be unnecessary in
stable BPH.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication and adverse effect profile. Trial step-down to single agent or cease
if no active urinary symptoms.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Risk of hypocalcaemia and fractures if delayed or missed. May be continued without
calcium/vitamin D monitoring.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure recent calcium and vitamin D levels are checked. Confirm ongoing need for
osteoporosis treatment and timely administration.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: Therapeutic Guidelines; AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Often used without confirmed deficiency. May be prescribed after past anaemia or
fatigue without ongoing indication.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text: Review pathology and clinical need. Cease if no deficiency or clinical rationale.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Can cause eye irritation, redness, and periocular changes. Continued long-term
without ophthalmology review.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Check if IOP is being monitored.
Ensure the resident or carers can administer drops correctly.
Confirm ongoing indication with ophthalmologist.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Therapeutic Guidelines – Eye

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Used as adjunct to statin or monotherapy for cholesterol control. May be continued
in frail patients without cardiovascular history.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review cardiovascular risk and life expectancy.
Cease if used for primary prevention in frail older adults without clear benefit.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: RACGP; AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
May be continued PRN without formal dry eye diagnosis. Can cause blurred vision if
overused.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure indication is documented (dry eye, blepharitis).
Rationalise to PRN if comfort-based use only.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Often used for arthritis pain, but risk of local irritation or confusion with systemic
NSAIDs.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure it's being applied properly.
Clarify if oral NSAIDs are also used to avoid double-up.
Trial cessation if ineffective.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Long-term therapy (>5 years) may increase risk of atypical femoral fractures or
osteonecrosis of the jaw.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review duration at 5 years.
Consider a “drug holiday” if BMD is stable and fracture risk low.
Ensure adequate calcium and vitamin D supplementation.
Arrange dental assessment before IV administration.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | RACGP Osteoporosis

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Delayed or missed injections (>7 months) may cause rebound vertebral fractures.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Maintain 6-monthly dosing.
If ceasing, transition to bisphosphonate cover to prevent rebound fractures.
Monitor calcium, vitamin D, and renal function.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | Therapeutic Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Limited cognitive benefit in advanced dementia; GI side effects common.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review every 6–12 months.
Trial withdrawal if cognition worsens or side effects outweigh benefit.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | Dementia Australia

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Limited evidence of benefit in late-stage dementia.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Continue only if measurable improvement in function or behaviour.
Cease if no clear benefit on review.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | Dementia Care Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Long-term use without active seizure disorder can cause sedation, confusion, or
hyponatraemia.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
If seizure-free >2 years, consider gradual taper with neurologist input.
Monitor sodium, liver function, and mood.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | eTG Neurology

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Tight glycaemic targets in frail older adults increase hypoglycaemia risk.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Aim for HbA1c 7–8.5%.
Stop sulfonylureas if recurrent low BGLs (<5 mmol/L).
Simplify to once-daily basal insulin if appropriate.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: RACGP Diabetes Guidelines | AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Absorption interference from calcium or iron; delayed TSH re-check.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Re-test TSH 6–8 weeks after dose change.
Separate from calcium or iron by ≥4 hours.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | Endocrine Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Renal decline or indefinite therapy without review.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review renal function every 6 months.
Ensure INR range (Warfarin) or CrCl dosing (DOAC) documented.
Reassess falls risk and benefit balance.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | RACGP Anticoagulation Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Continuing treatment when LDL <1.0 mmol/L and no cardiovascular history.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Consider dose reduction or cessation if risk low.
Repeat LFTs in 3 months.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | Lipid Management Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Prolonged use without gastroprotection; risk of renal injury.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Limit use to ≤4 weeks.
Add PPI for ≥65 yrs or dual antiplatelet/anticoagulant therapy.
Monitor creatinine and blood pressure.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | eTG Gastroenterology

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: May be duplicated with oral NSAIDs or used without benefit.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Confirm correct application.
Cease if ineffective.
Avoid concurrent systemic NSAID use.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Long-term exposure causes BMD loss, hyperglycaemia, and skin fragility.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review if >3 months therapy.
Monitor BMD, BP, and glucose.
Taper slowly when discontinuing.
Advise mouth rinse post-inhalation.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | COPD-X

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Tolerance, dependence, and falls risk in elderly residents.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Switch to diazepam equivalent.
Reduce total dose by 25% every 2 weeks.
Reinforce sleep hygiene and non-drug strategies.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH | RACGP | Deprescribing Network

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Abrupt withdrawal can trigger discontinuation syndrome.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text: If mood stable ≥6 months, taper gradually (–37.5 mg every 2–4 weeks for SNRIs).

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH

Annual Medication Governance Cycle:
Identify → Assess → Plan → Implement → Review (4–6 wks follow-up).
Medication Review Frequency Matrix:
Psychotropics – 3 mo
Anticoagulants / Antiplatelets – 6 mo
Cardiovascular – 12 mo
Antidiabetic – 6 mo
Anticonvulsants – 6–12 mo
Bone agents – 12 mo
Statins – 12 mo
NSAIDs – Each script
Opioids – 3–6 mo
Clinical Monitoring Checklist:
Cardiac – ECG, LFT, TFT every 6 mo
Endocrine – HbA1c, TSH every 6–12 mo
CNS – Falls, cognition every 3 mo
Bone – BMD, Vit D every 12–24 mo
Renal – eGFR, U&E every 6 mo
GI – B12, Mg every 12 mo

Part 5 – Practical Writing Tools (Tips + Tricks)

entries.title: 1. Cut the Waffle – Make Sentences Work Harder

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Long, passive, or repetitive sentences dilute your clinical message.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Rephrase to tighten and clarify. Use active voice.
Avoid saying the same thing twice (e.g. “It may be appropriate to consider trialling…”
→ "Trial may be appropriate").

entries.title: 2. Avoid “War on Paper” – Keep Reports Efficient

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Over-documenting or overexplaining makes reports harder to read and delays GP
response.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Use concise Issue → Action formatting. Don’t explain obvious things (e.g.
“paracetamol is often used for pain”). Focus on the resident-specific rationale.

Instead of:
•
"It may be worth considering..."
•
"Perhaps trialling..."
•
"We would recommend potentially discussing..."
Use:
•
“Trial [X] if appropriate”
•
“Cease if no recent use”
•
“Review ongoing benefit of [X]”

entries.title: 4. Watch for Passive Voice or Vague Intentions

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Saying “GP to consider possibly ceasing...” puts the onus back on the GP and
weakens the clinical suggestion.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
If you’re recommending something, just say it clearly.
“Cease if not required” is stronger than “GP may want to consider reviewing if
needed.”

entries.title: 5. Keep the Focus on the Resident – Always

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Statements like “this medication is often used...” are generic and weaken the case.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Refer to the resident by name (or “the resident”) and tie your reasoning to their
current condition.
“Joan has had no documented psychotic episodes in the last 12 months. Cease
Risperidone if not required.”

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Long-acting benzodiazepine with high risk of sedation, falls, and accumulation in
elderly. Not suitable for routine use in aged care.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Cease if no clear, documented indication.
Avoid PRN use for agitation or sleep. If used, monitor frequency and effect, and
document rationale and consent.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; TGA; Psychotropic Prescribing Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Potent long-acting benzodiazepine. Used for epilepsy or severe agitation but often
misused for sedation.
Oral liquid version is prone to dose confusion (mg vs mL vs drops).

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure indication is accurate and clearly documented.
Use standard units (mg or mL), not drops.
Monitor closely for over-sedation or confusion. Cease if used for BPSD without
psychiatric support.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; TGA; Australian Prescriber (Clonazepam oral liquid article)

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Shorter-acting benzodiazepine sometimes seen as “safer” but still carries sedation
and falls risk. PRN use often undocumented or excessive.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review effectiveness documentation and frequency of use.
Ensure consent is documented if used for BPSD.
Cease or restrict to time-limited PRN with review.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Psychotropic Use in Aged Care Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Intermediate-acting benzodiazepine. Commonly used for agitation, sleep, or
behavioural issues but with strong sedative profile.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Avoid regular use in dementia or frail elderly.
Review need and effectiveness of PRN doses.
Cease if used more than 3×/week without specialist review.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; TGA

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
SSRI often used long-term without recent review. May cause hyponatraemia,
sedation, or QT prolongation in elderly.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication and duration.
Check for side effects (falls, low sodium).
Consider trial reduction if stable >12 months and no recent depressive episodes.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; RACGP

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Long half-life SSRI with activating properties. Often used historically, but may not be
suitable in elderly due to insomnia, anxiety, and potential interactions.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review current need.
Consider switching if insomnia or restlessness present.
Monitor sodium levels and mental status. Cease if no recent depressive episodes.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; NPS MedicineWise

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Often prescribed for OCD or anxiety, but may contribute to sedation, dizziness, or
interaction with antipsychotics.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication and ongoing response.
Cease if no clear diagnosis or if other medications already address mood/anxiety.
Monitor for interaction with antipsychotics (e.g. risperidone).

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; TGA

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
SNRI often continued long-term without review. May raise blood pressure, cause
nausea, or impair cognition in elderly.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Check if resident still meets criteria for antidepressant.
Consider dose reduction or switch if sedation or side effects present.
Monitor BP, appetite, mood changes.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; RACGP

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Tricyclic antidepressant with strong anticholinergic effects. Can worsen confusion,
constipation, dry mouth, and falls.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Avoid use in dementia or delirium-prone residents.
Review need and trial taper if used for neuropathy or low mood.
Consider switch to non-sedating option or SNRI.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Beers Criteria

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
High anticholinergic load. Used off-label for pain, sleep, or mood but associated with
sedation, constipation, falls, and confusion.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Cease or replace if used for sleep or pain in frail residents.
Avoid in dementia.
Switch to Duloxetine or non-drug interventions if no clear benefit.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Therapeutic Guidelines – Pain; Beers Criteria

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Strong opioid with dual action (mu-opioid + noradrenaline). May cause sedation,
dizziness, and constipation. Often continued without reassessment.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review if pain is stable. Consider taper to 50–100 mg twice daily or switch to PRN.
Cease if no clear pain documentation or if sedation/falls noted.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Therapeutic Guidelines – Pain

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
High sedation and falls risk. Often prescribed as PRN and regular simultaneously,
leading to overdose risk.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Rationalise to one formulation only. Cease regular dosing if pain is not daily or
severe.
Ensure constipation management plan is in place.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; RACGP Prescribing in Older People

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Limited efficacy in elderly due to variable metabolism. Increases constipation and
sedation risk.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Cease if not clearly effective or if other opioids are also prescribed.
Avoid regular use. Switch to PRN paracetamol alone if mild pain.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Choosing Wisely Australia

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Potent opioid with short half-life. Often used in palliative care but continued beyond
needed timeframe. High risk of confusion and overdose in opioid-naïve residents.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure indication is appropriate.
Avoid in non-palliative contexts unless strictly needed.
Taper or cease if pain is stable or minimal.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Therapeutic Guidelines – Palliative Care

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Gold-standard opioid but not preferred in renal impairment due to active metabolite
accumulation and CNS toxicity.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Avoid in residents with eGFR <30 mL/min.
If used, document indication and reassess frequently.
Consider alternatives like oxycodone or buprenorphine patch if appropriate.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Renal Drug Database

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Long-acting opioid with complex pharmacokinetics and high risk of accumulation.
Should only be prescribed by experienced clinicians.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure specialist oversight (pain/palliative team or addiction medicine).
Avoid PRN use. Monitor sedation and QT interval if continued.
Do not initiate or titrate without appropriate authority and experience.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: TGA; AMH; Palliative Care Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Often continued as regular SR tablet in residents with difficulty swallowing. Liquid
forms may not be offered if SR is still charted.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Cease SR form if resident has swallowing issues.
Chart oral liquid as regular or PRN depending on pain pattern.
Avoid unnecessary duplication with PRN paracetamol.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Don’t Rush to Crush

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Frequent PRN use without documentation of effect may mask underlying pain
patterns or lead to excessive dosing.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Track frequency and effectiveness.
If used >3×/week, reassess need for regular dosing or non-drug interventions.
Always document reason and outcome after each PRN administration.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: Aged Care Quality Standards; AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Reserved for treatment-resistant schizophrenia. Requires strict haematological
monitoring. Risk of agranulocytosis, seizures, and cardiac effects.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure indication is current and regular full blood count monitoring is occurring.
Not to be initiated or adjusted in aged care without specialist input.
Document risks and ensure NOK consent is in place.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; TGA; Clozapine Monitoring Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Typicl antipsychotic used PRN for agitation or delirium. High risk of extrapyramidal
side effects (EPSE), QT prolongation, and sedation.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Use only short-term for delirium or psychosis.
Avoid routine PRN in dementia.
Document effect, dose, and reason if used acutely.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Delirium Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Second-gen antipsychotic with sedation and metabolic side effects. Often used off-
label for BPSD or agitation.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication.
Cease or reduce if no clear psychotic features.
Avoid long-term use unless benefit outweighs risk and consent is documented.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Psychotropic Use in Dementia Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Approved for short-term use in BPSD, but often continued longer or used as PRN
without adequate effect tracking.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure dose and duration follow TGA guidelines (max 12 weeks for BPSD).
Document reason and outcome for each PRN dose.
Obtain and review consent for ongoing use.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: TGA; AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Narrow therapeutic range, nephrotoxic, and prone to accumulation in elderly.
Requires regular monitoring (levels, renal function, thyroid).

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review serum levels and renal function 3-monthly.
Cease if toxicity risk high or no psychiatric review in >6 months.
Ensure hydration and avoid interacting drugs (e.g. NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors).

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Therapeutic Guidelines – Mood Disorders

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Used for epilepsy and mood stabilisation. Associated with liver toxicity,
thrombocytopenia, sedation, and weight gain.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review indication and effectiveness.
Monitor LFTs and platelets regularly.
Cease if no recent seizures or if alternative mood stabiliser preferred in elderly.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; TGA

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Used for epilepsy, mood, or neuropathic pain. Induces liver enzymes and interacts
with many drugs. Risk of hyponatraemia and sedation.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Check sodium and drug levels if used long-term.
Avoid polypharmacy and interacting psychotropics.
Cease if no longer effective or used off-label without review.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Therapeutic Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Used for bipolar depression and epilepsy. Risk of skin rash, especially if titrated too
quickly. Clearance reduced in renal impairment.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure slow titration if restarted.
Monitor for skin rash, sedation, and interactions with valproate.
Cease if no benefit or unmonitored use.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Mood Disorder Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Old-generation antiepileptic with narrow therapeutic range. Poor absorption and
high risk of toxicity in elderly.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Check levels and renal function routinely.
Cease if seizures are controlled and specialist review not ongoing.
Avoid in combination with interacting meds (e.g. warfarin, carbamazepine).

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Used in dementia with Parkinson's features or Lewy Body dementia. Can cause GI
upset, weight loss, and bradycardia.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Review if cognitive benefit is observed.
Monitor for falls, nausea, anorexia.
Cease if no clear benefit after 6 months or intolerable side effects.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Dementia Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Mirtazapine may assist with mood and sleep but offers limited benefit for chronic
pain. Duloxetine addresses both depression and neuropathic pain.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Taper mirtazapine gradually. Allow a 2–4 day washout.
Introduce duloxetine 30 mg daily. Monitor tolerability, mood, and pain response
within 2–4 weeks.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Therapeutic Guidelines – Pain & Depression

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Concurrent use of two sedatives increases risk of falls, sedation, and daytime
drowsiness.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Avoid concurrent prescribing unless sleep disorder is documented.
Trial cessation of temazepam and assess sleep chart. Reinforce non-pharmacological
sleep strategies.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Psychotropic Deprescribing Resources

entries.title: Duloxetine vs Amitriptyline for Pain in Frail Adults

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Amitriptyline has strong anticholinergic effects and is poorly tolerated in older adults.
Duloxetine may offer similar benefit with improved tolerability.
• Suggested Action:
Avoid initiating amitriptyline in frail residents.
Switch to duloxetine 30 mg daily if CrCl permits. Contraindicated by
manufacturer if CrCl<30 mL/min due to increased plasma concentration and
limited data.
.
Monitor falls, cognition, and mood response.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; Beers Criteria; RACGP Pain Guidelines

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Long-term benzodiazepine use for sleep is associated with dependence and falls.
Melatonin may offer a safer option.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Taper and cease benzodiazepine.
Introduce melatonin 2 mg MR at night.
Monitor over 1–2 weeks for sleep quality. Educate staff on sleep hygiene techniques.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: TGA; AMH; Dementia Australia

entries.title: Ceasing Long-Term Antidepressants in Stable Residents

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Antidepressants are often continued indefinitely despite remission. Older adults may
tolerate withdrawal well if stable for >12 months.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Taper slowly over 2–4 weeks.
Monitor mood and withdrawal symptoms.
Communicate clearly with GP and family.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: AMH; RACGP; Choosing Wisely Australia

entries.title: PRN Psychotropic Use – Frequency and Effectiveness

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
PRN sedatives (e.g. oxazepam, risperidone) are often used frequently without
documentation of effectiveness, indication, or outcome.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Monitor how often PRNs are given.
If used >3 times per week, reassess regular need.
Always document reason, effect, and non-pharmacological measures attempted.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: Aged Care Quality Standards; AMH

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Chemical restraint laws and aged care standards require documented consent for
regular and PRN psychotropics and high-risk opioids.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure signed consent is obtained for:
•
Regular psychotropics (e.g. risperidone, clonazepam)
•
PRN sedatives used for BPSD
•
Opioids used beyond 1–2 weeks
File documentation in the medication chart and care plan.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: ACQSC; Psychotropic Prescribing Guide

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
High-risk meds without NOK input may breach clinical governance expectations.
Many families are unaware of sedation risk.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Document discussions with NOK or EPOA for:
•
Long-term psychotropics
•
PRN use >1/week
•
Off-label medications
Keep a signed record and progress note summary.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: ACQSC; Residential Aged Care Consent Framework

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text:
Medications may be flagged as chemical restraints unless clearly linked to psychiatric
diagnosis.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Ensure BestMed or records include diagnosis such as:
•
“Schizoaffective disorder” or “Bipolar with aggression”
•
Not just “low mood” or “agitation”
If treating BPSD, confirm “dementia with psychosis” is documented.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: TGA; My Aged Care – Restraint Reporting Guidance

entries.title: Falls and Sedation Risks – Link to PRN Use

fields.label: Issue to Consider
fields.text: Falls often follow PRN use of sedatives, especially at night, yet not linked in reviews.

fields.label: Suggested Action
fields.text:
Audit all falls within 2 hours of PRN use.
Review whether alternative strategies were trialled.
Chart frequency, outcome, and time of administration in clinical reviews.

fields.label: Reference
fields.text: Aged Care Commission; Facility Falls Audits

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: No – slow-release

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: Tapentadol IR (crushable)

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Do not crush SR tablets — increased overdose risk.
Switch to immediate-release tablet if swallowing difficulty. Label clearly as non-crush
on med chart.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: No – modified-release

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text:
•
Oxycodone IR (crushable)
•
Oxycodone oral liquid

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Do not crush controlled-release formulations.
Confirm formulation with pharmacist if unsure.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: No – extended release

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text:
•
Hydromorphone IR (may be dispersed)
•
Subcutaneous available in palliative setting

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Always check if IR or ER version.
Do not crush Jurnista — overdose risk.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: No – modified-release

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text:
•
Ordine (oral liquid morphine)
•
IR tablets (crushable)

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Morphine liquid is preferred for swallowing issues.
Do not alter SR tablets without pharmacist advice.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: Partially – can be crushed, but bitter and nausea risk

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: Paracetamol liquid (codeine not available in liquid)

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Crushed tablets taste unpleasant.
Check for sedation or confusion in older adults.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: Yes – IR tablets can be crushed

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: Oral solution (hospital supply only)

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Can be crushed and mixed with soft food.
Do not confuse with XR (extended-release) – those should not be crushed.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: No – tablets not usually crushed

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: Risperidone oral liquid

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Use ODTtablet if swallowing issues.
Always use oral syringe for liquid – not teaspoons.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: Not recommended – bitter, dissolves poorly

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: ODT(Zydis wafers)

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Use wafers if resident cannot swallow tablets.
Wafers dissolve on the tongue – no water needed.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: No – highly lipophilic and unstable once crushed

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: Diazepam oral liquid, rectal gel (if prescribed)

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Liquid available in select formulations.
Ensure correct measurement in mL, not drops.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: No – tablets are not crushable

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: Oral liquid (0.1 mg/mL)

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Do not use drops — use syringe in mg or mL only.
Avoid confusing drops vs milligrams.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: Yes, but highly bitter

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: ODT available

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Use ODT formulation when swallowing is impaired.
ODT dissolves on tongue in seconds.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: IR tablets may be crushed; XR tablets must not be

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: Liquid formulation available (hospital supply or compounding)

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Only crush immediate-release (IR) metformin.
Do not crush XR – increased GI side effects and dose dumping risk.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: Yes – can be crushed

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: No oral liquid available

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Crush and mix with soft food.
Stable post-crushing, no special precautions.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: Yes – may be crushed

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: No liquid available

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Safe to crush and mix with small amount of food or water.
Monitor for hypotension after administration.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: Yes, but not ideal – bitter taste

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: No registered liquid formulations

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Can be crushed if needed, but taste may affect compliance.
Consider switching to an alternative if ongoing swallowing difficulty.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: Yes – can be crushed

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: Oral liquid available

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Crushing is acceptable and commonly done.
If liquid available, confirm concentration and syringe measurement.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: Yes – tablets may be crushed

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: Oral liquid or drops available

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Crush tablets with soft food or use oral liquid (measure in micrograms, not mL).
Ensure consistent dosing if using drops.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: Generally yes, but some are large and poorly palatable

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: Liquid multivitamins available

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Check product label – some contain enteric coatings.
If crushed, mix with food to mask flavour.

fields.label: Crushable
fields.text: No – many products are enteric-coated or soft capsules

fields.label: Alternative
fields.text: Liquid form available in some brands

fields.label: Notes for Nurses
fields.text:
Do not crush soft gels or coated tablets.
Use liquid if prescribed or consider ceasing if non-essential.

entries.title: Volume 3 – Part 2: eGFR-Based Dose Adjustment – Format

fields.text:
Each medication follows this structure:
•

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
•
Dose in Renal Impairment (based on eGFR)
•
Dose in Renal Replacement Therapy (RRT)
•

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text: Source: Renal Drug Database (RDD)

Renal Replacement Therapy (RRT) includes haemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis, used
when kidney function is severely reduced. These therapies can remove some
medications from the bloodstream while allowing others to accumulate. Because of
this, drug clearance, dosing intervals and toxicity risk can change significantly in
patients on RRT.
In this guide, “Dose in RRT” provides practical dosing considerations for residents
receiving maintenance haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis.

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Type 2 diabetes

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 500–2000 mg daily in divided doses

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Not metabolised; renally excreted unchanged

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
•
eGFR >45: No adjustment
•
eGFR 30–45: Max 1000 mg/day; caution
•
eGFR <30: Contraindicated (risk of lactic acidosis)

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not recommended in dialysis

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Contrast media (hold metformin for 48 hrs), NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor renal function every 3–6 months in elderly.
Consider alternative if GI side effects limit use.

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Atrial fibrillation, VTE prevention/treatment

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 5 mg twice daily

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Liver (CYP3A4) and renal (~27%)

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
•
Reduce to 2.5 mg BD if ≥2 of: age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, creatinine ≥133
μmol/L
•
Caution if eGFR <25

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not recommended in dialysis

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Azoles, macrolides, SSRIs, antiplatelets

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text: Monitor bleeding risk and renal function every 3–6 months.

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: AF with heart failure, rate control

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 62.5–250 mcg daily (adjusted by age/weight)

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: ~50–70% renal excretion

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
•
eGFR 30–50: Reduce to 125 mcg/day or alternate days
•
eGFR <30: 62.5 mcg every other day or less

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Use with extreme caution; monitor levels closely

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Amiodarone, verapamil, diuretics (hypokalaemia increases toxicity)

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor serum levels and electrolytes regularly.
Signs of toxicity: nausea, confusion, visual changes.

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: AF, DVT/PE prevention and treatment

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 20 mg once daily

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Liver and kidney (~33% renal excretion)

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
•
eGFR 30–49: Reduce to 15 mg daily
•
eGFR <30: Avoid in AF; possible use in VTE with caution

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not recommended in dialysis

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: SSRIs, azoles, NSAIDs, macrolides

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Avoid in patients with poor renal function unless no alternatives.
Monitor bleeding signs and renal function.

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Non-valvular AF, DVT/PE prevention

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 150 mg twice daily

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: 80% renal excretion (as unchanged drug)

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
•
eGFR 30–50: 110 mg twice daily
•
eGFR <30: Contraindicated

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not suitable

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: P-gp inhibitors (e.g. verapamil), SSRIs, NSAIDs

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Short half-life; missing doses increases stroke risk.
Monitor renal function regularly in elderly.

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Gout prevention, urate lowering

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 100–600 mg daily in 1–2 doses

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic and renal; active metabolite (oxypurinol) renally cleared

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
•
eGFR 30–59: Start at 50–100 mg daily
•
eGFR <30: Max 100 mg/day (adjust slowly upward based on urate)

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Start at 50–100 mg three times per week post-dialysis

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Azathioprine (severe toxicity), ampicillin (rash)

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Start low and go slow; monitor for rash (Stevens-Johnson), especially in renal
impairment.

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Moderate to severe pain, palliative care

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: Oral 5–60 mg/day in divided doses (SR/IR)

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic; active metabolites excreted renally

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
•
eGFR 30–59: Reduce dose and frequency
•
eGFR <30: Avoid or use very cautiously; monitor for toxicity

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Use alternatives (e.g. fentanyl, hydromorphone) preferred

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Sedatives, SSRIs, antipsychotics

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Accumulation leads to confusion, sedation, respiratory depression. Avoid if
alternatives exist.

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Hypertension, arrhythmias, angina

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 25–100 mg once daily

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: ~85% renally excreted unchanged

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
•
eGFR 30–60: Max 50 mg daily
•
eGFR <30: 25 mg daily or every second day

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: 25 mg post-dialysis or every 2nd day; monitor HR/BP

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other antihypertensives, digoxin

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text: Bradycardia and hypotension more likely in renal failure; titrate slowly.

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: VTE prophylaxis and treatment, ACS

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
•
Prophylaxis: 40 mg SC daily
•
Treatment: 1 mg/kg SC twice daily

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Renally excreted

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
•
eGFR 30–50: Use with caution
•
eGFR <30: 1 mg/kg once daily for treatment; 20–30 mg daily for prophylaxis

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Caution; use anti-Xa level monitoring if available

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other anticoagulants, SSRIs, NSAIDs

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text: Risk of bleeding increased in renal impairment. Avoid IM injections.

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Neuropathic pain, epilepsy

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 900–1800 mg/day in 2–3 divided doses

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Excreted unchanged in urine

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
•
eGFR 30–59: 200–700 mg/day
•
eGFR 15–29: Max 300 mg/day
•
eGFR <15: Max 100–300 mg every other day

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: 300 mg post-dialysis; adjust based on symptoms

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: CNS depressants, antacids (reduce absorption)

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Titrate dose based on efficacy and sedation. Reduce risk of falls by monitoring daily
function.
🟦 Amantadine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Parkinson’s disease, drug-induced extrapyramidal symptoms.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 100 mg 1–2 times daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Minimal hepatic metabolism; >90% renal excretion unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 30–50: 100 mg daily
eGFR 15–29: 100 mg every 2–3 days
eGFR <15: 100 mg every 7 days

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not effectively dialysed; same as eGFR <15.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Anticholinergics → confusion; psychotropics → hallucinations; QT-prolonging agents.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
High risk of confusion, hallucinations, falls in frail or CKD patients.
🟦 Amiodarone

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: Loading then 100–200 mg daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic; not renally cleared.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No change required.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed; no adjustment.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Warfarin, digoxin, beta-blockers, statins, azoles, macrolides.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Long half-life; monitor TFT/LFTs; avoid in severe bradycardia.
🟦 Bisoprolol

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Heart failure, hypertension, atrial fibrillation.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 2.5–10 mg daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: ~50% renal; ~50% hepatic.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 20–50: No change.
eGFR <20: Max 10 mg daily.
Severe CKD: Start low (1.25 mg).

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly removed; use same as eGFR <20.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Verapamil, diltiazem, amiodarone.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor HR, dizziness, fatigue.
🟦 Calcitriol

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: CKD-related hypocalcaemia, secondary hyperparathyroidism.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 0.25–0.5 micrograms daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic and extra-renal conversion; renal excretion of metabolites.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No dosage change required — titrate to calcium and PTH.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed; no adjustment.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Thiazides, calcium supplements, digoxin.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor calcium every 3 months; risk of hypercalcaemia.
🟦 Carbamazepine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Seizures, trigeminal neuralgia, mood stabilisation.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 200–1,200 mg/day in divided doses.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic; induces CYP enzymes.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No dose change typically required.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly dialysed; avoid extra doses.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: MAJOR inducer: lowers levels of warfarin, antipsychotics, antidepressants, DOACs.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor sodium (risk SIADH).
🟦 Carvedilol

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Heart failure, hypertension.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 3.125–25 mg twice daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic; renally excreted metabolites only.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No adjustment required.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Verapamil, diltiazem, amiodarone, digoxin.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor BP and dizziness, especially in frail or orthostatic patients.
🟦 Cefalexin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: UTIs, cellulitis, respiratory infections.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 250–500 mg every 6–12 hours.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Renal excretion unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Give dose after dialysis.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Warfarin (↑ INR), metformin.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Adjust for frailty to avoid neurotoxicity.
🟦 Clozapine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Treatment-resistant schizophrenia.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic (CYP1A2, CYP3A4).

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
No formal numeric adjustment.
In moderate–severe renal impairment (eGFR <30), start at the lower end of the
dosing range (e.g. 12.5 mg daily) and titrate more slowly.
Reduce total daily dose if excessive sedation, orthostatic hypotension or tachycardia
appear during titration.
Avoid rapid titration and avoid higher maintenance doses in severe CKD.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Smoking, fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor WCC, sedation, constipation, myocarditis.
🟦 Clonidine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Resistant hypertension, menopausal flushing, behavioural agitation.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 50–300 micrograms 2–3 times daily; patches weekly.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: ~40–60% renal excretion.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR <30: Reduce by ~50%.
Start low and titrate slowly.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not removed; same as eGFR <30.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Beta blockers (rebound hypertension risk), sedatives.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Avoid abrupt cessation.
🟦 Clopidogrel

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Antiplatelet therapy.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 75 mg daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic via CYP2C19.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No adjustment.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: PPIs (omeprazole), SSRIs, NSAIDs.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Bleeding risk increases in CKD despite no dose change.
🟦 Dapagliflozin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Type 2 diabetes (T2DM), symptomatic heart failure, chronic kidney disease.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 10 mg once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Extensively metabolised via UGT1A9 to inactive glucuronide; ~75% excreted in urine
(mostly as metabolites), ~21% in faeces.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 45–60: Dose as in normal renal function (glucose-lowering effect begins to
reduce).
eGFR 30–45: Dose as in normal renal function; glycaemic effect reduced but CV/renal
benefit persists.
eGFR 15–30: Dose as in normal renal function; do not rely on it for glucose control
alone.
eGFR <15: Dose as in normal renal function but do not initiate in this range.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
APD/CAPD, HD, HDF, CAV/VVHD: Unlikely to be dialysed – dose as per eGFR <15;
avoid starting in dialysis patients.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Insulin and sulfonylureas (↑ hypoglycaemia risk), diuretics
(↑dehydration/hypotension), lithium (↓ lithium levels).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Glucose-lowering effect is minimal when eGFR <45, but HF/CKD outcome benefit
remains. Monitor for volume depletion, AKI, and euglycaemic DKA (check ketones if
unwell).
🟦 Diazepam

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Anxiety, muscle spasm, status epilepticus, pre-operative sedation.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 2–10 mg orally, 1–4 times daily (depending on indication and frailty).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Hepatic metabolism to active metabolites; minimal renal excretion of unchanged
drug. Protein binding may fall and Vd may rise in ESRF.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR ≥30: Usually no formal adjustment, but start low and titrate slowly.
eGFR <10: Use small doses and titrate to response – accumulation and prolonged
sedation more likely.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
APD/CAPD, HD, HDF, CAV/VVHD: Not meaningfully dialysed – dose as for eGFR <10
and avoid repeated high doses.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other CNS depressants (opioids, antipsychotics), particularly clozapine or IM
olanzapine (risk of serious adverse effects), isoniazid, fluconazole/voriconazole,
ritonavir, sodium oxybate.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Renal impairment increases brain sensitivity → excessive sedation, encephalopathy.
Always have flumazenil available if using parenteral formulations; monitor closely in
frail or ESRF residents.
🟦 Donepezil

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Mild–moderate Alzheimer’s dementia.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 5–10 mg once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Hepatic (CYP3A4 and CYP2D6) to multiple metabolites; ~17% excreted unchanged in
urine. Long half-life (~70 h; unchanged in ESRF).

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 20–50: Dose as in normal renal function.
eGFR 10–20: Dose as in normal renal function.
eGFR <10: Dose as in normal renal function.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: APD/CAPD, HD, HDF, CAV/VVHD: Unlikely to be dialysed; no dose change.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other CYP3A4/2D6 substrates or inhibitors (e.g. some SSRIs, azoles, macrolides) –
may alter levels; additive bradycardia with beta-blockers.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor weight, heart rate, GI tolerance, and cognitive benefit. Consider
deprescribing if no clinically meaningful improvement in 6–12 months.
🟦 Duloxetine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text:
Depression, generalised anxiety, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, stress urinary
incontinence, chronic pain.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
Depression/anxiety: 60–120 mg daily.
Diabetic neuropathy: 60–120 mg daily (often in divided doses).
Incontinence: 20–40 mg twice daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Extensively metabolised in liver (CYP1A2, CYP2D6) to inactive metabolites; ~77%
excreted in urine as metabolites, <1% unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 30–50: Dose as in normal renal function but start low and titrate cautiously.
eGFR <30: Start at very low dose (e.g. 30 mg daily) and increase slowly according to
response; manufacturer is more conservative and often advises avoid if CrCl <30

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
APD/CAPD, HD, HDF, CAV/VVHD: Not dialysed/unlikely to be dialysed – dose as for
eGFR <30 with extra caution.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
SSRIs/SNRIs, NSAIDs, antiplatelets, anticoagulants (↑ bleeding risk), ciprofloxacin (↑
duloxetine levels; avoid), other CNS depressants.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Useful where mood + neuropathic pain overlap, but hyponatraemia, falls and GI
effects are concerns in frail CKD. Monitor sodium and mood; avoid in severe renal
impairment unless specialist-supervised.
🟦 Fentanyl

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text:
Acute procedural analgesia, ventilated patients, chronic intractable pain (including
patches).

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
IV bolus: 50–200 micrograms, then 25–50 micrograms as required.
IV infusion: 3–4.8 micrograms/kg/hour (spontaneous respiration), higher in assisted
ventilation.
Transdermal patches: 12–25 micrograms/hour initially, titrate every 72 hours.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Hepatic CYP3A4 to inactive metabolites; <7% excreted unchanged in urine. Half-life
may be prolonged in ESRF due to tissue redistribution.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 20–50: ~75% of normal dose; titrate to response.
eGFR 10–20: 75% of normal dose; titrate carefully.
eGFR <10: ~50% of normal dose (e.g. lower-strength patch or smaller oral doses),
titrate slowly.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
APD/CAPD, HD, HDF, CAV/VVHD: Not dialysed – use same dosing as eGFR <10 and
monitor closely for accumulation.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (azoles, macrolides, ritonavir) ↑ fentanyl levels; other CNS
depressants and antipsychotics ↑ risk of respiratory depression, hypotension, and
sedation.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Preferred strong opioid in advanced CKD compared to morphine due to lack of
active renally-cleared metabolites, but still high risk of sedation and falls in frail
residents. Your existing fentanyl patch “Issue to Consider” page fits well with this box.
🟦 Gabapentin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Neuropathic pain, epilepsy, uraemic pruritus (off-label in CKD).

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 900–1800 mg/day in 2–3 divided doses.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Not metabolised; excreted unchanged in urine.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 30–59: 200–700 mg/day.
eGFR 15–29: Max 300 mg/day.
eGFR <15: Max 100–300 mg every other day.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
For HD/HDF: 300 mg post-dialysis, then adjust dose based on pain/pruritus and
sedation.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
CNS depressants (opioids, sedatives) – ↑ risk respiratory depression and death in frail
CKD; antacids with aluminium/magnesium ↓ absorption; St John’s wort, some
antidepressants and antipsychotics can lower seizure threshold.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
For CKD neuropathic pain or uraemic pruritus, start lower than standard (e.g. 100 mg
after dialysis) and titrate slowly. Monitor gait, cognition, and falls risk closely.
🟦 Haloperidol

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Delirium, agitation, nausea, psychosis.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 0.5–5 mg orally/SC/IM depending on indication and frailty.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic (CYP3A4, CYP2D6). <1% excreted unchanged in urine.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 20–50: Dose as in normal renal function.
eGFR 10–20: Dose as in normal renal function.
eGFR <10:
Single doses OK,
For repeated dosing, start low, titrate cautiously due to risk of
accumulation/sedation.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly dialysed → use eGFR <10 approach.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Macrolides, azoles, antidepressants (QT prolongation), lithium, metoclopramide (EPS
risk).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Avoid in Parkinson’s or Lewy Body Dementia; higher delirium risk in CKD.
🟦 Hydromorphone
(Your Pain / Opioid rationalisation section references it as "safer than morphine in
CKD")

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Moderate–severe pain.

fields.label: Immediate-release
fields.text: 1–4 mg every 4–6 hours.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic to hydromorphone-3-glucuronide (neurotoxic metabolite) → renally cleared.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 20–50: Reduce dose by 25%.
eGFR 10–20: Reduce by 50%; extend dosing interval.
eGFR <10: Start LOW (0.5–1 mg) q6–8h; neurotoxicity risk ↑.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Partially removed by HD — give post-dialysis if needed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other CNS depressants, benzodiazepines, pregabalin/gabapentin, alcohol.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Preferred strong opioid in CKD vs morphine, but still can cause neurotoxicity due to
metabolite accumulation.
🟦 Hyoscine Butylbromide

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Abdominal colic, bowel obstruction, terminal secretions.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 10–20 mg SC/PO every 4 hours.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Minimal hepatic metabolism; excreted renally as metabolites.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 20–50: Dose as normal.
eGFR 10–20: Dose as normal.
eGFR <10: Dose as normal.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
