fields.text: Not significantly dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other anticholinergics → ↑ confusion, constipation, retention.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor for anticholinergic burden, particularly in constipation or glaucoma.
🟦 Hyoscine Hydrobromide

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Motion sickness, palliative secretions.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 300–600 micrograms every 6 hours.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic and renal; small portion excreted unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
Same dosing across all eGFR bands.
BUT use caution in frail CKD due to CNS penetration → delirium/hallucinations.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other anticholinergics; sedatives.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Higher delirium risk than glycopyrrolate because it crosses BBB.
🟦 Irbesartan
(ACEI/ARB section in your Toolbox)

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Hypertension, diabetic nephropathy, heart failure.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 75–300 mg daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic (CYP2C9), excreted in urine and faeces.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 20–50: Dose as normal.
eGFR 10–20: Dose as normal.
eGFR <10: Start low (75 mg daily) — titrate slowly.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: ACEI, K⁺-sparing diuretics, NSAIDs → ↑ hyperkalaemia/AKI.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor K⁺ and creatinine 1–2 weeks after dose changes.
🟦 Lamotrigine
(In your mood stabiliser / antiepileptic crossover section)

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Epilepsy, bipolar depression.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: Typical maintenance 100–200 mg/day (slow titration).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic glucuronidation; metabolites excreted renally.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 20–50: Dose as normal.
eGFR <20: Reduce maintenance by ~50%.
eGFR <10: Reduce further; titrate slowly.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Hemodialysis removes 20–30% → may require small post-HD supplemental doses.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Valproate (doubles levels), carbamazepine (lowers levels), sertraline, oral
contraceptives.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Higher risk of rash/SJS with rapid titration.
🟦 Levetiracetam
(You use it in seizure / delirium differential notes)

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Epilepsy, adjunct anticonvulsant.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 500–1500 mg twice daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Not hepatically metabolised; ~66% excreted unchanged in urine.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 50–80: 500–1000 mg BD
eGFR 30–50: 250–750 mg BD
eGFR 15–30: 250–500 mg BD
eGFR <15: 250–500 mg daily

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Give 250–500 mg post-dialysis.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Few significant interactions; sedation ↑ with any other CNS depressant.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Good option for seizures in ESRF patients due to predictable renal clearance.
🟦 Levodopa / Carbidopa
(Parkinson’s therapy section)

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Parkinson’s disease.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 100/25 mg three times daily (titrated individually).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Peripheral decarboxylation; renal excretion of metabolites.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No adjustment required across all eGFR levels.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Antipsychotics (blocks effect), MAO inhibitors, antihypertensives (postural
hypotension).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor for hallucinations, confusion, postural hypotension in CKD.
🟦 Lisinopril

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Hypertension, heart failure.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 2.5–40 mg daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Not metabolised; entirely renally excreted unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 20–50: Start lower (2.5–5 mg).
eGFR 10–20: 2.5 mg daily.
eGFR <10: Avoid or use with extreme caution.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Partially dialysed → supplement post-HD if needed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: K⁺-sparing diuretics, ARBs, NSAIDs.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor K⁺/creatinine 1–2 weeks after initiation or dose increase.
🟦 Lithium
(You include this under “High-Risk / Rare Medications”)

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Bipolar disorder.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: Serum-level guided (usually 400–1200 mg/day).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Not metabolised; 95% renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 45–59: Reduce dose by 25%.
eGFR 30–44: Reduce dose by 50%.
eGFR <30: Avoid if possible.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Removed during dialysis → levels fall significantly; specialist dosing required.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: ACEI/ARB, NSAIDs, diuretics (esp. thiazides), carbamazepine, SSRIs.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Extremely narrow therapeutic window; monitor levels + renal function every 3
months.
🟦 Metformin
(You cover MR crushing + dose reduction in CKD)

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Type 2 diabetes.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 500–2000 mg/day (divided).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Not metabolised; 90–100% renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR ≥45: Full dose.
eGFR 30–45: Max 1000 mg/day; monitor 3–6 monthly.
eGFR <30: Avoid (lactic acidosis risk).

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Avoid.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Iodinated contrast (stop 48h), topiramate, cimetidine.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
In frail RACF residents with low appetite → higher lactic acidosis risk.
🟦 Metoprolol
(Seen often in your Heart Failure combo examples)

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Hypertension, AF rate control, heart failure (metoprolol succinate).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic (CYP2D6); minimal renal excretion.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No adjustment required.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: SSRIs (fluoxetine, paroxetine ↑ levels), amiodarone, verapamil/diltiazem.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor HR, dizziness, fatigue, especially during up-titration.
🟦 Nortriptyline

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression, neuropathic pain

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
25–75 mg daily (often at night), up to 150 mg/day in divided doses; lower doses in
older adults

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Extensive hepatic metabolism (CYP2D6); only a small amount excreted unchanged in
urine

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
• eGFR 30–60: No formal adjustment; start low (10–25 mg nocte) and titrate slowly
• eGFR 15–29: Usually no dose change needed; consider lower target dose and
slower titration
• eGFR <15: Start at the lowest dose (10–25 mg nocte) and titrate cautiously; monitor
for anticholinergic effects, confusion, QT prolongation

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
No specific adjustment; start low and titrate carefully in HD/CAPD as drug is not
significantly dialysed

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
SSRIs, other TCAs, MAOIs, tramadol, anticholinergics, antiarrhythmics (QTc), CYP2D6
inhibitors (e.g. fluoxetine, paroxetine)

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
High anticholinergic and sedation burden; avoid high doses in frail older adults and
pre-existing conduction disease.
🟦 Olanzapine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, adjunct in depression

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 5–20 mg once daily (lower starting doses in older adults)

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic metabolism (mainly CYP1A2, UGT); <10% excreted unchanged in urine

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
• eGFR 30–60: Dose as in normal renal function; consider starting 2.5–5 mg nocte
• eGFR 15–29: Dose as in normal renal function but start low and titrate slowly
• eGFR <15: Use lowest effective dose (e.g. 2.5–5 mg nocte); monitor sedation,
hypotension and EPS

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
Not significantly removed by HD or CAPD; dose as per corresponding eGFR category
and clinical response

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
CNS depressants, benzodiazepines, carbamazepine (↓ levels), fluvoxamine (↑ levels),
smoking (↑ clearance), dopamine agonists (antagonism)

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
High metabolic risk (weight, lipids, glucose); monitor for stroke risk in dementia and
for chemical restraint classification in aged care.
🟦 Oxycodone

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Moderate–severe pain (acute and chronic)

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
Short-acting: 5–10 mg every 4–6 hours PRN
SR: total daily dose divided BD

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4, CYP2D6) to active and inactive metabolites; ~8–14%
excreted unchanged in urine

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
• eGFR 30–59: Dose as normal but start at lower end (e.g. 2.5–5 mg q6h) and titrate
slowly
• eGFR 15–29: Reduce total daily dose by ~25–50%; extend dosing interval (e.g. q6–
8h)
• eGFR <15: Use ~50% of usual dose with longer intervals; avoid SR preparations if
possible; monitor for sedation and respiratory depression

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
HD/HDF: Drug and metabolites are dialysable; consider small supplemental dose
post-HD based on pain and sedation. CAPD/APD: variable removal—dose as per
eGFR <15 and monitor closely

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other opioids, benzodiazepines, gabapentinoids, alcohol, CYP3A4
inhibitors/inducers, serotonergic antidepressants (serotonin toxicity risk with high
doses/combination)

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
High risk of accumulation, falls and confusion in CKD; consider alternatives (fentanyl,
hydromorphone, buprenorphine) in advanced renal failure.
🟦 Oxazepam

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Anxiety, short-term management of insomnia

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
Anxiety: 15–30 mg three to four times daily (elderly: 10–20 mg tds/qid)
Insomnia: 15–50 mg at night

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Conjugated in liver to inactive glucuronides; metabolite excreted renally

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
• eGFR 30–59: Dose as in normal renal function
• eGFR 15–29: Dose as in normal renal function but favour lower starting doses in
older adults
• eGFR <15: Start at lowest possible dose (e.g. 7.5–10 mg) and titrate cautiously due
to metabolite accumulation and prolonged half-life

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
HD/APD: Not significantly dialysed → use same approach as eGFR <15; avoid regular
high doses

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other CNS depressants (opioids, antipsychotics, antihistamines, alcohol), rifampicin (↓
effect), cimetidine (↑ levels), clozapine (↑ serious CNS adverse effects)

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Preferred benzo in liver disease, but still increases falls, delirium and restraint risk in
aged care—aim for PRN, short courses at lowest dose.
🟦 Paracetamol

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Pain, fever

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: Up to 1 g every 4–6 hours PRN; maximum 4 g/day (lower in frail/low weight)

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic glucuronidation and sulfation; <5% excreted unchanged in urine

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
• eGFR 30–59: Dose as in normal renal function
• eGFR 15–29: Dose as normal but extend interval to q6h; consider max 3 g/day
• eGFR <15: 500–1000 mg every 6–8 hours; max 3 g/day; watch for accumulation
with long-term use

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
HD/HDF: Paracetamol is dialysed; dose as for eGFR <15 and consider 500–1000 mg
post-HD if needed. APD: not significantly dialysed; dose as eGFR <15.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Chronic alcohol use, enzyme inducers (e.g. carbamazepine, phenytoin), warfarin (with
prolonged high-dose use)

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
First-line analgesic in CKD; keep under 60 mg/kg/day and lower max daily dose (e.g.
3 g) in frail or malnourished residents.
🟦 Pregabalin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Neuropathic pain, focal seizures, generalised anxiety disorder

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 150–600 mg/day in 2–3 divided doses

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Minimally metabolised; ~90% excreted unchanged in urine

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
(Use total daily dose, then divide BD/TDS)
• eGFR 30–59: Max ~300 mg/day
• eGFR 15–29: Max ~150 mg/day
• eGFR <15: 25–75 mg once daily (or 25–50 mg BD if very symptomatic)

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
HD: Give 25–75 mg post-dialysis only; adjust based on pain, sedation and falls.
CAPD/APD: similar to eGFR <15, titrating carefully

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other CNS depressants (opioids, benzos, z-drugs, antihistamines), alcohol; may
potentiate opioid-related respiratory depression and falls

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Very renally cleared—major accumulation in CKD; taper slowly to avoid rebound
anxiety/insomnia, and review regularly for efficacy vs harms.
🟦 Quetiapine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text:
Schizophrenia, bipolar disorder (mania/depression), adjunct in major depression, off-
label for insomnia/BPSD

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
Schizophrenia/mania: 300–800 mg/day
Bipolar depression / MDD adjunct: 50–300 mg/day (usually nocte)

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Extensive hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4); <5% excreted unchanged in urine

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
• eGFR 30–59: Same target doses but start 25 mg/day and increase by 25–50 mg/day
as tolerated
• eGFR 15–29: Dose as in normal renal function with low starting dose and slow
titration
• eGFR <15: Continue low-and-slow approach; no formal adjustment but monitor
closely for sedation, hypotension and falls

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
Not significantly dialysed; dose as per eGFR category and clinical response (no
specific adjustment)

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
CYP3A4 inhibitors (azoles, macrolides, protease inhibitors), CYP3A4 inducers
(carbamazepine, phenytoin), other QT-prolonging drugs, CNS depressants

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
In BPSD/insomnia it is usually a chemical restraint unless clearly documented as
treatment of a psychotic disorder—review indication and dose regularly.
🟦 Rivaroxaban

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Atrial fibrillation (stroke prevention), DVT/PE treatment and prophylaxis

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
AF: 20 mg once daily with food
DVT/PE treatment: 15 mg twice daily for 3 weeks, then 20 mg once daily

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4, CYP2J2) and renal excretion; ~36% excreted
unchanged in urine

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
• eGFR ≥50: Standard doses as above
• eGFR 15–49: AF – reduce to 15 mg once daily; for VTE use with caution and
individualise (specialist advice)
• eGFR <15: Avoid; DOACs generally contraindicated in this range

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not recommended in dialysis; warfarin or specialist-guided alternatives preferred

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors (azoles, protease inhibitors, some macrolides), strong
inducers (carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampicin), antiplatelets, NSAIDs, SSRIs/SNRIs

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Clearance reduced in severe renal impairment—bleeding risk increases as eGFR falls.
Re-check renal function at least every 3–6 months in older adults.
🟦 Risperidone

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text:
Schizophrenia, psychosis, bipolar mania, persistent aggression in Alzheimer’s
dementia

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
Oral: 2–6 mg/day (max 16 mg/day) in 1–2 doses
Depot: 25–50 mg IM every 2 weeks; Okedi 75–100 mg every 28 days

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Hepatic metabolism to active 9-hydroxyrisperidone; ~70% of active moiety excreted
renally

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
• eGFR 30–59: Start lower (e.g. 0.25–0.5 mg BD, titrate slowly); usual max often 3–4
mg/day in frail older adults
• eGFR 15–29: Reduce target dose; titrate slowly (clearance ↓ by ~60% in severe RI)
• eGFR <15: Use very low doses (e.g. 0.25–0.5 mg once or twice daily) and titrate
cautiously; monitor closely for EPS, sedation and postural drop

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
HD removes a modest amount (≈25% of 3 mg BD over 5 hours); no standard
supplemental dosing—dose based on clinical response and adverse effects

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
CYP2D6/3A4 inhibitors (fluoxetine, paroxetine, some antivirals), carbamazepine (↓
levels), other QT-prolonging drugs, CNS depressants, levodopa/dopamine agonists
(antagonism)

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Higher EPS and stroke risk in dementia; document indication vs restraint, use
minimum effective dose, and review frequently in CKD due to reduced clearance.
🟦 Tacrolimus

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text:
Calcineurin inhibitor for prophylaxis and treatment of acute rejection in kidney, liver
and heart transplantation; moderate–severe atopic eczema (topical/oral specialist
use).

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
Doses are highly individual and protocol-driven.
Typical initial oral doses (transplant):
– Kidney: 0.2–0.3 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses
– Liver: 0.1–0.2 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses
– Heart: ~0.075 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses
Adjust to target trough levels as per transplant unit.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Extensive hepatic metabolism via CYP3A4; <1% excreted unchanged in urine. Highly
protein-bound and distributed in erythrocytes.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 20–50: Dose as in normal renal function (monitor levels and renal function).
– eGFR 10–20: Dose as in normal renal function.
– eGFR <10: Dose as in normal renal function; close monitoring due to
nephrotoxicity.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
– HD, HDF, CAPD/APD, CVVH/CAV/VVHD: Not dialysed/unknown dialysability; dose
as in normal renal function, titrated to levels.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (azoles, macrolides, some antivirals, grapefruit) ↑ tacrolimus
levels and toxicity.
CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John’s wort) ↓ levels and ↑
rejection risk.
Additive nephrotoxicity with aminoglycosides, amphotericin, NSAIDs, trimethoprim,
etc.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Therapeutic drug monitoring essential; narrow index and large inter-patient
variability. Different brands are not interchangeable.
🟦 Tadalafil

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text:
Erectile dysfunction (ED), benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), pulmonary arterial
hypertension (PAH).

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
– ED: 10–20 mg at least 30 minutes before sexual activity; max once daily.
– BPH: 5 mg once daily.
– PAH: 40 mg once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Hepatic metabolism via CYP3A4 to inactive metabolite; ~36% excreted in urine
(mostly metabolites), remainder in faeces.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 30–50:
• ED: 5–10 mg, not more often than every 48 hours.
• BPH: 2.5–5 mg daily.
• PAH: 20–40 mg daily.
– eGFR <30:
• ED: 5–10 mg, not more often than every 72 hours, use with caution.
• BPH & PAH: Avoid (manufacturer).

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
– HD: Not dialysed; use ED dosing as for eGFR <30; avoid for BPH/PAH.
– CAPD/APD, HDF, CVVH: Unlikely/not dialysed; dose as per eGFR band (usually <30).

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (azole antifungals, macrolides, HIV protease inhibitors,
cobicistat) ↑ tadalafil levels.
Nitrates, nicorandil, riociguat and α-blockers ↑ risk of profound hypotension –
generally avoid. Grapefruit juice may ↑ levels.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
AUC is roughly doubled in moderate–severe renal impairment; protein binding
unchanged.
🟦 Tamoxifen

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Hormone-receptor–positive breast cancer; anovulatory infertility.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
– Breast cancer: 20 mg once daily.
– Anovulatory infertility: 20–80 mg daily on days 2–5 of cycle.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Extensive hepatic metabolism (CYP-mediated) to active metabolites (e.g. endoxifen);
excreted mainly via faeces as conjugates, with minor renal excretion.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 20–50: Dose as in normal renal function.
– eGFR 10–20: Dose as in normal renal function.
– eGFR <10: Dose as in normal renal function.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
– HD, HDF, CAPD/APD, CVVH: Unknown dialysability; dose as in normal renal
function.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Potent CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g. fluoxetine, paroxetine, bupropion, some other
antidepressants) may reduce conversion to active metabolite and reduce efficacy.
Potentiates coumarin anticoagulants; monitor INR. Terbinafine may reduce tamoxifen
efficacy.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Has been used in encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis in PD patients (20 mg daily) –
niche but relevant in renal cohort.
🟦 Tamsulosin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) – LUTS.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 400 micrograms once daily after breakfast.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Hepatic metabolism via CYP2D6 and CYP3A4; excreted mainly in urine as metabolites
with small proportion unchanged. Highly protein-bound.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 20–50: Dose as in normal renal function.
– eGFR 10–20: Dose as in normal renal function.
– eGFR <10: Dose as in normal renal function; use with caution.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
– CAPD/APD, HD, HDF, CVVH: Not/unknown dialysability; dose as for eGFR <10 or
10–20 mL/min.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Additive hypotension with antihypertensives, diuretics, β-blockers, other α-blockers
and PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, etc). Ketoconazole ↑ tamsulosin levels.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
In CKD, monitor for postural hypotension and falls, particularly when combined with
other vasodilators. Protein binding ↑ in renal impairment.
🟦 Tapentadol

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text:
Moderate–severe acute (and chronic) pain – μ-opioid agonist + noradrenaline
reuptake inhibitor.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
– IR: 50 mg every 4–6 hours; max 600 mg/day (700 mg on day 1).
– SR: start 50 mg twice daily; max 500 mg/day.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Predominantly hepatic glucuronidation to inactive conjugates; ~70% excreted in
urine as metabolites, ~3% unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 20–50: Dose as in normal renal function.
– eGFR 10–20: Dose as in normal renal function (monitor sedation and accumulation).
– eGFR <10: Use smaller doses with extended dosing intervals; titrate to effect and
tolerability.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
– HD, CAPD/APD, HDF, CVVH: Probably dialysed; base dosing on eGFR <10–20 band
and titrate; monitor for withdrawal and analgesic failure on dialysis days.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Additive CNS and respiratory depression with other opioids, benzodiazepines,
sedating antihistamines, antipsychotics, alcohol.
Serotonergic agents (SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, MAOIs) ↑ risk of serotonin toxicity and
seizures.
UGT inducers (rifampicin, St John’s wort, phenobarbital) ↓ effect; UGT inhibitors
(azole antifungals) ↑ levels.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Manufacturer does not recommend use in severe renal impairment due to limited
data – if used, employ extreme caution and close monitoring.
🟦 Telmisartan

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text:
Angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) – hypertension; prevention of cardiovascular
events.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
– Hypertension: 20–80 mg once daily.
– CV event prevention: 80 mg once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Hepatic glucuronidation to inactive conjugate; almost entirely excreted in faeces via
bile as unchanged drug; minimal renal excretion.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 20–50: Dose as in normal renal function.
– eGFR 10–20: Dose as in normal renal function.
– eGFR <10: Start 20 mg once daily and up-titrate cautiously according to BP and
renal function.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
– CAPD/APD, HD, HDF, CVVH: Not/rarely dialysed; dose as for eGFR <10–20 mL/min
with careful K+ and creatinine monitoring.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Additive renal impairment and hyperkalaemia with ACEIs, other ARBs, NSAIDs,
ciclosporin, tacrolimus, potassium-sparing diuretics and potassium salts. May ↑
digoxin levels.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Hyperkalaemia and AKI are more common in pre-existing renal impairment and
bilateral renal artery stenosis or single kidney. Close monitoring after initiation and
dose changes.
🟦 Temazepam

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Short-term insomnia; pre-medication anxiolysis before minor procedures.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
– Insomnia: 10–40 mg at night.
– Premed: 20–40 mg 30–60 minutes before procedure.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Hepatic metabolism to inactive glucuronide conjugates; ≥80% of metabolites
excreted in urine; <2% excreted unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 20–50: Dose as in normal renal function.
– eGFR 10–20: Dose as in normal renal function but start at small doses.
– eGFR <10: Dose as in normal renal function but start low; monitor for prolonged
sedation and delirium.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: – CAPD/APD, HD, HDF, CVVH: Not/rarely dialysed; dose as for eGFR <10 mL/min.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Additive CNS depression with opioids, antipsychotics, sedating antidepressants,
antihistamines, alcohol. Rifampicin may ↑ metabolism; ritonavir and disulfiram may ↑
levels/toxicity.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Increased CNS sensitivity in CKD; long-term use risks dependence and withdrawal –
particularly problematic in dialysis cohort.
🟦 Terbinafine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Systemic and topical antifungal for skin and nail dermatophyte infections.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
– Oral: 250 mg once daily.
– Topical: apply once or twice daily (renal function not relevant).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Extensive hepatic metabolism to inactive metabolites; ~80% of these are renally
excreted; no unchanged drug in urine. Clearance ~50% lower when GFR <50 mL/min.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
Dose in RRT
fields.text:
– CAPD/APD, HD, HDF, CVVH: Unlikely/unknown dialysability; dose as for eGFR <20
mL/min and monitor closely for toxicity.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
CYP inducers (rifampicin) ↓ terbinafine exposure; CYP inhibitors (cimetidine, azoles,
amiodarone) ↑ levels. Potent inhibitor of CYP2D6 – may ↑ levels of TCAs, β-blockers,
some SSRIs and antiarrhythmics.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Manufacturer often contraindicates use in severe renal impairment due to limited
data; use only if benefit outweighs risk, with monitoring in CKD 4–5.
🟦 Tiotropium

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text:
Long-acting antimuscarinic bronchodilator – maintenance treatment of COPD (and
asthma in some protocols).

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
– Handihaler: 18 micrograms inhaled once daily.
– Respimat: 5 micrograms inhaled once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Largely excreted unchanged in urine (around 14% of inhaled dose). Some
metabolism via CYP2D6/CYP3A4 and non-enzymatic hydrolysis.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 20–50: Dose as in normal renal function.
– eGFR 10–20: Dose as in normal renal function; use with caution.
– eGFR <10: Dose as in normal renal function; use with caution (↑ exposure).

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
– CAPD/APD, HD, HDF, CVVH: Unknown dialysability; dose as in normal renal
function but monitor for anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, urinary retention).

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Avoid combination with other anticholinergics due to additive effects. Increased risk
of antimuscarinic side-effects with disopyramide and similar agents.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Half-life is prolonged in renal impairment; clinical trials suggest generally safe but
accumulation is possible, so watch for urinary retention and glaucoma symptoms in
CKD.
🟦 Tacrolimus

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Transplant rejection prophylaxis, autoimmune conditions.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: Highly individual; typically 0.05–0.3 mg/kg/day.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic CYP3A4; <1% renally cleared.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No adjustment — but nephrotoxic; requires level monitoring.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed; dose guided by trough levels.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Azoles, macrolides, protease inhibitors, grapefruit (↑ levels);
Phenytoin, rifampicin, carbamazepine (↓ levels).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor renal function, BP, glucose, electrolytes.
🟦 Tadalafil

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: ED, BPH, pulmonary hypertension.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
ED: 10–20 mg PRN.
BPH: 5 mg daily.
PAH: 40 mg daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic CYP3A4; metabolites excreted in urine and faeces.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 30–50:
– ED: 5–10 mg every 48 hrs
– BPH: 2.5–5 mg daily
eGFR <30:
– ED: 5–10 mg every 72 hrs
– Avoid for BPH/PAH.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed; use severe CKD dosing.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Nitrates, PDE-5 inhibitors, α-blockers, CYP3A4 inhibitors.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Higher exposure in CKD → hypotension risk increases.
🟦 Tamoxifen

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: ER+ breast cancer, ovulation induction.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 20 mg daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic CYP2D6/CYP3A4; minimal renal clearance.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No adjustment required at any stage.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (fluoxetine, paroxetine) reduce efficacy.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor for VTE, endometrial cancer risk, and menopausal symptoms.
🟦 Tamsulosin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Benign prostatic hyperplasia.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 400 micrograms after breakfast daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic CYP3A4/CYP2D6; metabolites renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No adjustment required, including severe CKD.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed; standard dosing.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: PDE-5 inhibitors, antihypertensives → hypotension risk.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Caution in orthostatic hypotension and fall-prone residents.
🟦 Tapentadol

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Moderate–severe pain (acute or chronic).

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
IR: 50 mg q4–6h;
SR: 50 mg BD, max 500 mg/day.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic glucuronidation; ~3% unchanged renal.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 20–50: No change.
eGFR 10–20: No change, monitor sedation.
eGFR <10: Reduce dose and extend interval.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Likely dialysed; dose as for eGFR <10.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Opioids, benzos, antidepressants (serotonin toxicity), alcohol.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Use extreme caution in end-stage CKD due to limited evidence.
🟦 Telmisartan

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Hypertension, cardiovascular risk reduction.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 20–80 mg daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic glucuronidation; minimal renal clearance.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR ≥10: No change.
eGFR <10: Start at 20 mg daily; titrate cautiously.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: ACEIs, ARBs, NSAIDs, K+ supplements → hyperkalaemia risk.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor K+ and renal function 1–2 weeks after initiation.
🟦 Temazepam

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Short-term insomnia.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 10–40 mg nocte.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic metabolism; metabolites renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No adjustment — but start low due to prolonged sedation.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: CNS depressants, opioids, antipsychotics.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
High fall and delirium risk in older adults/CKD.
🟦 Terbinafine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Fungal skin/nail infections.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 250 mg daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic; metabolites renally cleared.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: eGFR <50: Reduce to 125 mg daily or 250 mg alternate days.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed; same as severe CKD.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: CYP2D6 inhibition ↑ levels of TCAs, β-blockers, SSRIs.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Avoid if severe CKD unless essential.
🟦 Tiotropium

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: COPD, asthma maintenance.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
18 micrograms inhaled once daily (HandiHaler)
5 micrograms daily (Respimat).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Mostly renally excreted unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No adjustment — but use caution in eGFR <50 due to ↑ exposure.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Dialysability unknown; no change.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other anticholinergics.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor for urinary retention, dry mouth, glaucoma symptoms.
🟦 Topiramate

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Epilepsy, migraine prevention.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 50–400 mg/day in divided doses.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Renal excretion of unchanged drug.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: eGFR <70: Use 50% of normal dose.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Dialysed — give supplemental dose post-HD.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Valproate (hyperammonemia risk), OCPs (reduced efficacy).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor bicarbonate; risk of metabolic acidosis.
🟦 Tramadol

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Moderate pain.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic CYP2D6/CYP3A4; renally excreted metabolites.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly removed; use eGFR <10 dosing.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs (serotonin toxicity), antipsychotics (seizures).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Avoid SR formulations in CKD stage 4–5.
🟦 Tranexamic Acid

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Bleeding, surgical prophylaxis.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 0.5–1 g every 8 hours (IV/PO, indication-specific).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Mostly renally excreted unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 20–50: Reduce frequency to q12h.
eGFR 10–20: q24h.
eGFR <10: Reduce dose by 50%.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Dialysed — dose after dialysis.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Combined hormonal contraceptives, pro-thrombotic agents.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor VTE risk in immobilised or CKD residents.
🟦 Trimethoprim

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: UTI treatment/prophylaxis.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
200 mg BD (treatment).
100 mg nocte (prophylaxis).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Partially hepatic; ~60% renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 15–25: Consider dose reduction.
eGFR <15: Use 50–100% of normal dose.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
HD: Give after dialysis.
PD: Not dialysed; use reduced dose.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: ACEIs/ARBs, spironolactone → severe hyperkalaemia risk.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Avoid with eGFR <15 if possible due to ↑ K+ and ↑ creatinine.
🟦 Valaciclovir

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: HSV, VZV, CMV prophylaxis.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 500–1000 mg 1–3 times/day (indication-dependent).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Converted to acyclovir; renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 30–50: Reduce frequency.
eGFR 10–30: Major reduction.
eGFR <10: Once daily or less (indication-specific).

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Dialysed — give post-HD.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other nephrotoxins, cimetidine, probenecid (↑ levels).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Risk of neurotoxicity in CKD (confusion, tremor).
🟦 Valganciclovir

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: CMV treatment and prophylaxis.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 900 mg daily (prophylaxis), 900 mg BD (treatment).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Converted to ganciclovir; renally cleared.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: Detailed step-down based on eGFR (full → half → every 48h).

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Often given post-HD, 450 mg 1–3× weekly.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Myelosuppressive agents, zidovudine, didanosine.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor FBC; high risk neutropenia.
🟦 Valsartan

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Hypertension, heart failure.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Minimal hepatic; excreted in bile.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: eGFR ≤20: Start 40 mg/day and titrate.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: K+/K-sparing diuretics, NSAIDs, ACEIs.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor renal function and K+ after dose changes.
🟦 Zopiclone

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Short-term insomnia.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 3.75–7.5 mg at night.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic metabolism; inactive metabolites renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
No formal adjustment, but in eGFR <30 start at 3.75 mg and avoid regular long-term
use.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly dialysed; same as severe CKD dosing.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other CNS depressants (opioids, benzos, antipsychotics, antihistamines), alcohol.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
High falls and delirium risk in older adults; treat as a chemical restraint if used long-
term for “behaviour” rather than insomnia with consent.
🟦 Zolpidem

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Short-term insomnia.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 5–10 mg at night (older adults usually 5 mg).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Extensive hepatic metabolism; minimal unchanged renal excretion.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
No dose adjustment required, but in eGFR <30 use 5 mg max and avoid ongoing
use.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly dialysed; no extra dosing.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other sedatives, opioids, alcohol; additive CNS depression.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Can cause sleep-walking, confusion, and “hangover” sedation; avoid in dementia /
high falls risk residents.
🟦 Sertraline

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression, anxiety disorders, PTSD, OCD.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 50–200 mg once daily (start 25–50 mg).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic (CYP2B6, 2C19, 3A4); metabolites renally excreted but largely inactive.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No formal adjustment; in eGFR <30 start low (12.5–25 mg) and titrate slowly.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly dialysed; usual doses with “start low, go slow”.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other serotonergic drugs (SNRIs, TCAs, tramadol, linezolid), MAOIs, St John’s wort,
anticoagulants/antiplatelets (↑ bleed risk).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Often first-line SSRI in CKD; monitor sodium (hyponatraemia), GI effects and falls.
🟦 Escitalopram

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression, anxiety disorders.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 10–20 mg once daily (older adults often 5–10 mg).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic (CYP2C19, 2D6, 3A4); metabolites renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 30–60: No change, but start 5 mg.
eGFR <30: Avoid high doses; usually max 10 mg daily.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed to a clinically relevant extent; same as severe CKD dosing.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other QT-prolonging drugs, serotonergic agents, MAOIs; CYP2C19 inhibitors may ↑
levels.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Lower QT risk than citalopram but still monitor ECG at higher doses in frail residents.
🟦 Citalopram

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression, anxiety.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 20–40 mg once daily (older adults: max 20 mg).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic (CYP2C19, 3A4, 2D6); metabolites renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
Mild–moderate CKD: no formal change, but avoid >20 mg in older adults or eGFR
<30.
Severe CKD (eGFR <15): consider 10–20 mg max with ECG monitoring.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly dialysed; dose as per severe CKD guidance.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other QT-prolonging agents, MAOIs, triptans, tramadol; CYP2C19 inhibitors ↑ QT risk
via higher levels.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
High QT concern; prefer sertraline/escitalopram in frail CKD.
🟦 Fluoxetine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression, OCD, bulimia, panic disorder.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 20–60 mg once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic CYP2D6; very long half-life; active metabolite (norfluoxetine).

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
No formal dose change, but in eGFR <30 keep doses low (e.g. 20 mg) due to long
half-life and accumulation.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed; no extra dosing, effects persist for weeks.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Potent CYP2D6 inhibitor – ↑ levels of TCAs, some antipsychotics, metoprolol; interacts
with tamoxifen (↓ effectiveness); serotonergic combinations.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Because of long half-life, not ideal if frequent changes required; can be useful where
adherence is erratic.
🟦 Paroxetine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression, anxiety disorders, OCD, PTSD.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 20–50 mg once daily (older adults lower).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic (CYP2D6) with some renal excretion.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 30–60: Start 10–20 mg; often keep at lower end.
eGFR <30: Reduce dose by ~50% (e.g. 10 mg daily) and titrate cautiously.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly removed; use CKD dosing with close monitoring.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Potent CYP2D6 inhibitor, similar to fluoxetine; serotonergic combinations; tamoxifen
interaction (↓ efficacy).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
More anticholinergic and weight gain; tends to be less favoured in frail older CKD
patients.
🟦 Fluvoxamine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression, OCD, anxiety.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 50–300 mg/day in divided doses (often nocte in older adults).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic (CYP1A2, 2D6, 2C19); negligible renal excretion unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No formal adjustment, but in eGFR <30 start low and monitor.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Strong inhibitor of multiple CYPs – ↑ levels of clozapine, warfarin, theophylline, TCAs,
some benzos.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Because of interaction profile, use cautiously in polypharmacy / transplant /
clozapine patients.
🟦 Venlafaxine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression, generalised anxiety, panic disorder, neuropathic pain.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 75–225 mg/day (usually XR once daily).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic to active metabolite (O-desmethylvenlafaxine); both renally cleared.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 30–59: Reduce total daily dose by ~25%.
eGFR 15–29: Reduce by ~50% (e.g. max 112.5 mg XR).
eGFR <15: Use low doses only (e.g. 37.5–75 mg/day) or consider alternative.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Some removal in HD; base dose on eGFR category and give after dialysis if needed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other serotonergic drugs, MAOIs, tramadol; may ↑ BP at higher doses.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
At high doses in CKD, toxicity risk rises (BP, agitation, withdrawal)
🟦 Desvenlafaxine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 50 mg once daily (most patients).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Minimal hepatic metabolism; largely renally excreted unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 30–50: 50 mg once daily.
eGFR <30: 50 mg on alternate days (or 25 mg daily if available).

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
In ESRF on HD: 50 mg every second day or small doses post-dialysis guided by
tolerability.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other serotonergic agents, MAOIs, tramadol; additive bleed risk with
anticoagulants/antiplatelets.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Renal clearance makes dose reduction essential in CKD; withdrawal symptoms if
stopped abruptly.
🟦 Duloxetine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression, GAD, diabetic neuropathy, chronic pain, stress incontinence.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 60–120 mg daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic (CYP1A2, 2D6); metabolites renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 30–60: No formal change but start at 30 mg and titrate slowly.
eGFR <30: Generally avoid or use very low doses with specialist oversight.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed to a useful extent; avoid in dialysis patients if possible.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
CYP1A2 and 2D6 inhibitors/inducers; serotonergic agents;
anticoagulants/antiplatelets (↑ bleed risk).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Hyponatraemia, hepatotoxicity, and BP changes more problematic in frail CKD.
🟦 Mirtazapine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression, insomnia, appetite stimulation.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 15–45 mg at night.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic (CYP1A2, 2D6, 3A4); ~75% excreted in urine as metabolites.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
eGFR 30–60: Usually no change; start at 15 mg.
eGFR <30: Consider lower starting dose (7.5–15 mg) and lower max dose.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly dialysed; use CKD dosing and watch for accumulation.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other CNS depressants, MAOIs, serotonergic agents; additive sedation with benzos,
opioids, antipsychotics.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Good for poor appetite/insomnia but can worsen weight gain, daytime sedation and
falls in CKD.
🟦 Vortioxetine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 10–20 mg once daily (start 5–10 mg in older adults).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic (CYP2D6 mainly; also 3A4, 2C9); metabolites excreted via urine and faeces.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
No dose adjustment required across CKD stages, but in eGFR <30 consider starting 5
mg and titrate based on tolerability.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly removed by dialysis; no extra dose.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (fluoxetine, paroxetine, quinidine) may require lower dose;
serotonergic combinations.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Low sexual side-effect and weight profile; fits nicely in your “newer antidepressant”
section with minimal renal adjustment.
🟦 Agomelatine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Depression (melatonin receptor agonist / 5-HT2C antagonist).

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 25–50 mg at night.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Extensive hepatic metabolism (CYP1A2, 2C9, 2C19); metabolites renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
No specific adjustment for mild–moderate CKD; limited data in severe CKD – use
cautiously or avoid if eGFR <30.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Very limited data; generally avoid in dialysis.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Potent CYP1A2 inhibitors (fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin) markedly ↑ levels; avoid.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Liver monitoring essential (LFTs); less commonly used in RACF.
🟦 Morphine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Moderate–severe pain, palliative care.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
2.5–10 mg every 4 hours (immediate-release) or sustained-release preparations twice
daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Hepatic metabolism to morphine-3-glucuronide and morphine-6-glucuronide; both
renally excreted and accumulate in renal impairment.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
Avoid routine use if eGFR <30.
If required:
– eGFR 30–60: Use 25–50% of usual dose.
– eGFR <30: Avoid due to high neurotoxicity and respiratory depression risk.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not effectively dialysed. Avoid use in dialysis-dependent patients.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other CNS depressants, benzodiazepines, gabapentinoids, antipsychotics, alcohol.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
High risk of confusion, agitation, myoclonus and sedation in CKD. Strongly avoid in
older adults with eGFR <30.
🟦 Codeine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Mild–moderate pain, cough suppression.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 15–60 mg every 4–6 hours.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Prodrug converted via CYP2D6 to morphine; renally cleared metabolites.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 30–60: Reduce dose by 25–50%.
– eGFR <30: Avoid due to accumulation of active metabolites.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not recommended. Metabolites accumulate despite dialysis.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: CYP2D6 inhibitors (fluoxetine, paroxetine), other sedatives, alcohol.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Unreliable analgesia in older adults, slow metabolism, and high risk of toxicity in CKD.
🟦 Buprenorphine

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Chronic pain, opioid dependence, transdermal analgesia.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
5–40 micrograms/hour transdermal patch applied weekly; sublingual formulations for
dependence.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic metabolism; minimal renal elimination of active metabolites.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No adjustment required across all CKD stages.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly removed by dialysis; no dose adjustment.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other CNS depressants, benzodiazepines, alcohol.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Preferred strong opioid in CKD. Ceiling effect for respiratory depression provides
safety advantage.
🟦 Fentanyl

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Severe chronic pain, palliative care, breakthrough pain.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
Transdermal patch 12–100 micrograms/hour changed every 72 hours;
buccal/intranasal for breakthrough use.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic CYP3A4; inactive metabolites.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No adjustment required. Safe in severe CKD.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed; no dose change.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (azole antifungals, macrolides, protease inhibitors) may
increase levels.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Good option for CKD 4–5 where morphine and codeine are inappropriate.
🟦 Methadone

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Chronic pain, opioid dependence, palliative care.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: Highly individualised. Typically 2.5–10 mg every 8–12 hours when used for pain.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Extensive hepatic metabolism; minimal renal clearance.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
No adjustment generally required, but initiate at low doses and titrate slowly due to
long half-life.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly removed by dialysis; no extra dosing required.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
QT-prolonging drugs, CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers, other serotonergic or sedating
medications.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Complex pharmacokinetics. Requires specialist oversight due to variable half-life and
QT prolongation risk.
🟦 Aripiprazole

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, adjunct in major depression, irritability in autism.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 10–30 mg once daily (often start at 5–10 mg in older adults).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Extensive hepatic metabolism (CYP2D6 and CYP3A4); minimal renal excretion of
unchanged drug.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
No formal adjustment required, including moderate–severe CKD. In eGFR <30, start
at lower doses (2.5–5 mg) and titrate cautiously.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly dialysed; no dose adjustment.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluoxetine, paroxetine, fluvoxamine, azoles,
macrolides) may increase levels; inducers (carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampicin) may
reduce effect.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Lower metabolic and QT risk than many antipsychotics but can cause akathisia and
insomnia. Useful where sedation is not desired.
🟦 Paliperidone

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
Oral modified-release: 3–12 mg once daily.
Depot: doses vary by product and interval.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Active metabolite of risperidone; largely excreted unchanged in urine; clearance is
proportional to renal function.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
Oral:
– eGFR 50–80: Use lower starting dose (e.g. 3 mg daily, cautious titration).
– eGFR 10–50: Reduce dose by about 50% and titrate slowly.
– eGFR <10: Generally avoid oral paliperidone.
Depot:
– Long-acting injections are usually contraindicated or require major reduction when
CrCl <50; specialist advice required.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
Not effectively removed by dialysis; avoid depot preparations in dialysis patients
unless under specialist supervision.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other QT-prolonging drugs, CNS depressants, dopamine agonists (antagonism).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Because it is renally cleared, accumulation in CKD markedly increases EPS, prolactin
elevation, and QT risk.
🟦 Lurasidone

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Schizophrenia, bipolar depression.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 40–160 mg once daily with food (at least 350 kcal).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4); metabolites excreted in urine and faeces.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– Mild impairment (eGFR ≥50): No change.
– Moderate to severe (eGFR 15–49): Lower starting dose and maximum dose (for
example, do not exceed 80 mg/day).
– eGFR <15: Generally avoid due to limited data.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Limited data; usually avoided in dialysis patients.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin) contraindicated; strong
CYP3A4 inducers (carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampicin) reduce efficacy.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Favourable metabolic profile compared with some other antipsychotics, but renal
limits on maximum dose need clear documentation.
🟦 Ziprasidone

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Schizophrenia, acute mania, agitation.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
Oral: 40–160 mg/day in divided doses with food.
IM for acute agitation: dose per protocol.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Primarily hepatic; about two-thirds hepatic metabolism, one-third renal excretion of
metabolites; very little unchanged drug.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
No formal adjustment for oral therapy. In eGFR <30, start at low doses and monitor
QT and orthostatic BP.
IM: use cautiously in CKD with lower doses.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not significantly removed by dialysis.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Other QT-prolonging drugs, strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
High QT risk relative to some other agents; not usually first-line in frail or renally
impaired older adults.
🟦 Sodium Valproate (Valproic Acid)

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Epilepsy, bipolar disorder, migraine prophylaxis.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
Usually 500–2,000 mg/day in divided doses; adjusted to serum levels and clinical
response.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Extensive hepatic metabolism; metabolites excreted renally. Protein binding
decreases in renal impairment, increasing free fraction.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
No formal dose adjustment, but lower albumin and reduced clearance mean free
drug is higher; start at lower doses and titrate to clinical response and, if available,
free valproate levels.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
Some removal by dialysis, but not usually enough to require extra dose unless levels
are low; dosing guided by levels and seizures.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Lamotrigine (increases lamotrigine levels), carbamazepine, phenytoin, aspirin, other
highly protein-bound drugs.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor LFTs, platelets and ammonia. Use caution in older adults and those with liver
disease.
🟦 Gabapentin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Neuropathic pain, focal seizures, uraemic pruritus (off-label).

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 900–1800 mg/day in 2–3 divided doses.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Not metabolised; excreted unchanged by the kidneys.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
Total daily dose (divide BD or TDS):
– eGFR 30–59: 200–700 mg/day.
– eGFR 15–29: 100–400 mg/day.
– eGFR <15: 100–300 mg every other day or very low daily dosing.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
Haemodialysis removes drug; often give 100–300 mg after each dialysis session and
titrate to symptoms and sedation.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other CNS depressants (opioids, benzodiazepines, z-drugs, antipsychotics); antacids
with aluminium or magnesium can reduce absorption.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
High risk of sedation, ataxia and falls in CKD, particularly when combined with
opioids. Start very low and titrate slowly.
🟦 Phenytoin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Seizures, status epilepticus, sometimes neuropathic pain.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: Usually 200–400 mg/day in divided doses; guided by serum levels.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Hepatic metabolism with saturable (non-linear) kinetics; highly protein bound;
minimal renal excretion of unchanged drug.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
Total level can be misleading because protein binding falls and free fraction rises. No
fixed dose adjustment but:
– Use lower doses and
– Interpret levels using corrected or free phenytoin concentrations.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
Some removal by haemodialysis but usually not enough to require routine extra
dosing. Adjust according to measured levels and clinical state.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Potent inducer of many CYP enzymes (warfarin, steroids, antipsychotics,
antidepressants, DOACs). Interacts with valproate, carbamazepine, some antibiotics
and antifungals.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Narrow therapeutic index, high interaction burden. In older CKD patients, often
preferable to use alternatives such as levetiracetam.
🟦 Digoxin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Atrial fibrillation rate control, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 62.5–250 micrograms once daily depending on age, weight and indication.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Predominantly renally excreted unchanged; clearance closely related to GFR.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 20–50: 125–250 micrograms daily.
– eGFR 10–20: 62.5–125 micrograms daily.
– eGFR <10: 62.5 micrograms daily or on alternate days; monitor levels.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
Dialysis does not reliably remove digoxin; dose as per eGFR <10 and monitor serum
levels closely.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Amiodarone, verapamil, diltiazem, macrolides, diuretics causing electrolyte
disturbance, some antiarrhythmics.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Narrow therapeutic window. Watch for toxicity: anorexia, nausea, confusion, visual
disturbances, bradyarrhythmias, especially in CKD.
🟦 Atenolol

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Hypertension, angina, rate control in atrial fibrillation.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 25–100 mg once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Minimally metabolised; mostly excreted unchanged by kidneys.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 30–60: May use full dose with monitoring.
– eGFR 15–30: Reduce dose (for example 25–50 mg daily).
– eGFR <15: 25 mg daily or less; titrate to heart rate and BP.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
Some removal by dialysis; usually dose after haemodialysis and monitor BP and heart
rate.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other rate-limiting agents (verapamil, diltiazem), amiodarone, drugs that mask
hypoglycaemia symptoms.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Because it is renally cleared, there is greater risk of bradycardia and hypotension in
CKD than with more hepatically cleared beta-blockers.
🟦 Sotalol

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Atrial and ventricular arrhythmias.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: Typically 40–160 mg twice daily (initiated and adjusted under specialist supervision).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Not significantly metabolised; largely excreted unchanged in urine.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 40–60: Extend dosing interval or reduce dose.
– eGFR 30–40: Once-daily dosing at lower dose.
– eGFR <30: Generally avoid due to high risk of accumulation and torsades de
pointes.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text:
Partially dialysed; use extreme caution and usually avoid in dialysis unless managed
by cardiology with close QT and level monitoring.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Other QT-prolonging drugs, diuretics that cause hypokalaemia or
hypomagnesaemia, other beta-blockers.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Because of strong renal dependence and QT risk, sotalol is usually avoided in
moderate–severe CKD in favour of other antiarrhythmics.
🟦 Furosemide

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Oedema, heart failure, fluid overload, hypertension (less effective alone).

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 20–40 mg once or twice daily; higher doses in fluid overload.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Partial hepatic metabolism; majority excreted unchanged in urine.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
Loop diuretics remain effective in CKD.
– eGFR 30–60: May require higher doses (40–80 mg).
– eGFR <30: Often require significantly higher doses (80–240 mg/day).
Dose guided by response and electrolytes.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not dialysed; dosing based on residual urine output.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: ACE inhibitors/ARBs, digoxin (electrolyte disturbance), other nephrotoxins.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor potassium, sodium, magnesium, and volume status. Ineffective for BP
control alone in advanced CKD.
🟦 Spironolactone

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Heart failure, resistant hypertension, ascites, hyperaldosteronism.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 12.5–50 mg once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic metabolism to active metabolites; renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 45–60: Use 12.5–25 mg daily.
– eGFR 30–45: Avoid doses >25 mg; monitor potassium within 1 week.
– eGFR <30: Generally avoid due to hyperkalaemia risk.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Avoid unless under specialist supervision with close potassium monitoring.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, potassium supplements, NSAIDs, trimethoprim.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
High risk of hyperkalaemia in older adults and CKD. Check electrolytes regularly.
🟦 Amiloride

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Adjunct diuretic for potassium conservation, heart failure, hypertension.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 5–10 mg once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Minimally metabolised; renally excreted unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 30–60: Use with caution, reduce dose.
– eGFR <30: Avoid due to high risk of hyperkalaemia.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Contraindicated; accumulation and severe hyperkalaemia risk.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, spironolactone, NSAIDs, potassium supplements.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Rarely used in frail older adults; potassium-sparing effect can be dangerous.
🟦 Hydrochlorothiazide / Indapamide (Thiazide Diuretics)

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Hypertension, mild oedema.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5–25 mg daily.
Indapamide 1.25–2.5 mg daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Indapamide hepatic; hydrochlorothiazide renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR >30: Usual dosing.
– eGFR <30: Thiazides largely ineffective; avoid or switch to loop diuretics.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not effective in dialysis patients.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Lithium, digoxin (electrolyte disturbance), corticosteroids.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Monitor electrolytes (hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia). Indapamide often preferred for
older adults.
🟦 Dapagliflozin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Type 2 diabetes, heart failure, CKD progression delay.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 10 mg once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic metabolism; inactive metabolites renally excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR ≥45: Full dose 10 mg daily.
– eGFR 25–44: Continue for HF or CKD but minimal glycaemic effect.
– eGFR <25: Initiation not recommended; continuation allowed for HF/CKD
indications per guidelines.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not recommended; avoid in dialysis.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Diuretics (volume depletion), insulin/SU (hypoglycaemia risk).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Reduce risk for HF and CKD progression even at low eGFR. Watch for genital
infections, dehydration.
🟦 Empagliflozin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Type 2 diabetes, heart failure, CKD.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 10–25 mg once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Hepatic glucuronidation; metabolites excreted renally.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR ≥45: Full dose.
– eGFR 20–44: Glycaemic effect reduced, but continue for HF/CKD benefit.
– eGFR <20: Avoid initiation.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Not recommended.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Diuretics, insulin/SU, nephrotoxins.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Preferred SGLT2 for cardiorenal protection. Monitor for dehydration.
🟦 Sitagliptin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Type 2 diabetes.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 100 mg once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Minimal hepatic metabolism; 80% renally excreted unchanged.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR ≥45: 100 mg daily.
– eGFR 30–44: 50 mg daily.
– eGFR <30: 25 mg daily.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: 25 mg daily; small dialysis clearance.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Sulfonylureas/insulin (hypoglycaemia risk).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Well tolerated in older adults; low hypoglycaemia risk when not combined with
insulin.
🟦 Linagliptin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Type 2 diabetes.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 5 mg once daily.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Enterohepatic elimination; negligible renal clearance.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text: No dose adjustment required at any CKD stage.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: No dose change; not dialysed.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: P-gp inhibitors/inducers, other diabetes medications.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Preferred DPP-4 inhibitor in advanced CKD.
🟦 Semaglutide (Ozempic)

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Type 2 diabetes, weight reduction.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 0.25 mg weekly → 0.5 mg → 1 mg weekly (or 2 mg depending on product).

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Proteolytic degradation; minimal renal clearance.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
No adjustment required.
Monitor hydration; GI side effects worse in CKD.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: No dose change required; limited experience.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Delays gastric emptying (affects absorption of oral meds).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
GI intolerance common; caution with frailty and weight loss in RACF.
🟦 Insulin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: Individualised based on regimen and glucose monitoring.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Cleared by kidney and liver.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
Insulin requirements decrease as GFR falls.
– eGFR 30–60: Reduce total daily dose by 25%.
– eGFR <30: Reduce dose by up to 50%; monitor for hypoglycaemia.
– Tight titration required.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Insulin sensitivity varies; frequent glucose checks essential.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Beta-blockers (mask hypoglycaemia), corticosteroids (increase glucose), SGLT2
inhibitors.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
High risk of hypoglycaemia in CKD; simplify regimens where possible.
🟦 Amoxicillin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Broad-spectrum penicillin for respiratory, urinary, skin and other bacterial infections.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text: 250–1000 mg every 8 hours depending on indication and severity.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text: Partly metabolised; 60–70% excreted unchanged in urine.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR 30–60: Usual dose, but consider 8–12 hourly intervals.
– eGFR 10–30: 250–500 mg every 12 hours.
– eGFR <10: 250–500 mg every 24 hours.

fields.label: Haemodialysis
fields.text: give dose after dialysis; typical 250–500 mg every 24 hours.

fields.label: Peritoneal dialysis
fields.text: dose as for eGFR <10.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Allopurinol (rash), warfarin (INR fluctuation), methotrexate (reduced clearance).

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Generally safe in CKD; main concerns are dose-dependent GI effects and rare
crystalluria at very high doses.
🟦 Amoxicillin–Clavulanate

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text:
Broad-spectrum penicillin plus β-lactamase inhibitor for resistant respiratory, skin,
urinary and intra-abdominal infections.

fields.label: Dose in Normal Renal Function
fields.text:
500/125 mg every 8–12 hours or 875/125 mg every 12 hours; higher IV doses for
severe infection.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Amoxicillin renally excreted unchanged; clavulanate partly metabolised and renally
excreted.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
Oral dosing:
– eGFR 30–60: 500/125 mg every 12 hours.
– eGFR 10–30: 500/125 mg every 12–24 hours.
– eGFR <10: 500/125 mg every 24 hours; avoid high-strength 875/125 tablets.

fields.label: Haemodialysis
fields.text:
500/125 mg every 24 hours plus an extra 250–500/125 mg dose after
dialysis.

fields.label: Peritoneal dialysis
fields.text: 500/125 mg every 24 hours.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text: Warfarin (INR fluctuation), allopurinol (rash), methotrexate.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Higher rates of GI upset and cholestatic hepatitis. Use shortest effective course in
older adults and CKD.
🟦 Nitrofurantoin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text: Lower urinary tract infection; prophylaxis in recurrent UTI.

fields.label: Immediate-release
fields.text:
50–100 mg every 6 hours (treatment) or 50–100 mg once daily at
night (prophylaxis).
Modified-release preparations dosed twice daily depending on product.

fields.label: Metabolism
fields.text:
Partially metabolised; rapidly excreted in urine via glomerular filtration and tubular
secretion.

fields.label: Dose in Renal Impairment (eGFR)
fields.text:
– eGFR ≥45: Standard dosing.
– eGFR 30–44: Short-course use (3–7 days) may be considered if benefits outweigh
risks.
– eGFR <30: Avoid; inadequate urinary concentrations and increased systemic
toxicity.

fields.label: Dose in RRT
fields.text: Avoid in dialysis patients.

fields.label: Important Drug Interactions
fields.text:
Antacids containing magnesium trisilicate may reduce absorption; probenecid and
sulfinpyrazone reduce renal excretion and increase toxicity risk.

fields.label: Other Information
fields.text:
Risk of pulmonary toxicity, peripheral neuropathy and hepatotoxicity is higher in
renal impairment and older adults. Not suitable for pyelonephritis or systemic
infection.
🟦 Ciprofloxacin

fields.label: Clinical Use
fields.text:
